frames.text: ing tank in which the hull or body acts as the structural frame of the

frames.name: p011-text-1002
frames.text: tractor, as well as the housing for the propelling and fighting units

frames.name: p011-text-1003
frames.text: and crews. It differs from previous and other types of tractors and

frames.name: p011-text-1004
frames.text: self-propelling land units in that it has no chassis or supporting frame

frames.name: p011-text-1005
frames.text: structure, but more closely resembles marine structure, in that the

frames.name: p011-text-1006
frames.text: hull carries with it the entire mechanism and all of the running gear

frames.name: p011-text-1007
frames.text: except the track links which pass around the hull in the form of a

frames.name: p011-text-1008
frames.text: continuous belt on each side of the machine.

frames.name: p011-text-1009
frames.text: Propulsion on the Mark VIII machine is secured by taking the

frames.name: p011-text-1010
frames.text: drive from a 12-cylinder Liberty engine through a planetary gear

frames.name: p011-text-1011
frames.text: box, thence through a chain drive, which in turn actuates the driving

frames.name: p011-text-1012
frames.text: sprocket of the track. As the track is propelled continuously around

frames.name: p011-text-1013
frames.text: the machine, it carries with it sections of the rail over which the

frames.name: p011-text-1014
frames.text: rollers, upon which the machine runs, travel. The length of the track

frames.name: p011-text-1015
frames.text: belt allows the machine to accommodate itself to inequalities of the

frames.name: p011-text-1016
frames.text: ground, while at the same time providing a rail surface for the

frames.name: p011-text-1017
frames.text: supporting rollers.

frames.name: p011-text-1018
frames.text: The machine is 34 feet 2½ inches in length, 12 feet in width, and

frames.name: p011-text-1019
frames.text: the over-all height is 10 feet 3 inches. The engine and driving

frames.name: p011-text-1020
frames.text: members, including the clutch, the epicyclic transmission and chain

frames.name: p011-text-1021
frames.text: drive, are located in the rear of the hull. The engine together with

frames.name: p011-text-1022
frames.text: the clutch and epicyclic gearing and other necessary engine parts

frames.name: p011-text-1023
frames.text: occupy the engine room, which is 9 feet 9 inches in length.

frames.name: p011-text-1024
frames.text: HULL LAYOUT

frames.name: p011-text-1025
frames.text: From the rear of the engine room back to the center of the track-

frames.name: p011-text-1026
frames.text: driving wheel is 4 feet 8⅛ inches. In front of the engine room is

frames.name: p011-text-1027
frames.text: the fighting and operating room, at the forward end of which is the

frames.name: p011-text-1028
frames.text: driver’s seat with the control levers. On either side of the fighting

frames.name: p011-text-1029
frames.text: compartment there is a sponson or projecting swinging structure

frames.name: p011-text-1030
frames.text: carrying a 6-pounder gun. The sponsons contain gun mountings

frames.name: p011-text-1031
frames.text: capable of giving a wide radius of fire with the 6-pound guns. In

frames.name: p011-text-1032
frames.text: addition, the sponsons themselves may be swung back into the

frames.name: p012-text-1090
frames.text: Surmounted above the fighting compartment is the main turret

frames.name: p012-text-1091
frames.text: which carries five machine guns. Above the main turret is the

frames.name: p012-text-1092
frames.text: directing officer’s coning tower from which it is possible to obtain

frames.name: p012-text-1093
frames.text: vision on all sides of the machine and from which its movements may

frames.name: p012-text-1094
frames.text: be directed. Located in the fighting compartment are sufficient

frames.name: p012-text-1095
frames.text: ammunition storage provisions for both 6-pounder and machine guns.

frames.name: p012-text-1096
frames.text: Entrance to the fighting compartment is secured through a door on

frames.name: p012-text-1097
frames.text: either side and in the doors there are also mounted machine guns.

frames.name: p012-text-1098
frames.text: This gives a total of seven machine guns, five being in the main

frames.name: p012-text-1099
frames.text: turret and two in the doors; and two 6-pounders, one located in each

frames.name: p012-text-1100
frames.text: sponson.

frames.name: p012-text-1101
frames.text: The fighting compartment is separated from the engine room by a

frames.name: p012-text-1102
frames.text: bulkhead in which there are sliding doors.

frames.name: p012-text-1103
frames.text: The exterior portion of the hull is elongated on each side to provide

frames.name: p012-text-1104
frames.text: a guide for the track. The rear extremity contains the chain housing

frames.name: p012-text-1105
frames.text: for the chain drive and the track driving sprocket and the forward

frames.name: p012-text-1106
frames.text: extremity carries the track adjusting wheel which can be moved for-

frames.name: p012-text-1107
frames.text: ward or backward to tighten or loosen the track chain.

frames.text: Steering is accomplished by allowing the track on one side to move

frames.name: p013-text-1120
frames.text: at a faster rate than the track on the other which tends to swing

frames.name: p013-text-1121
frames.text: the machine in the direction of the slow-moving track. If one track

frames.name: p013-text-1122
frames.text: is locked and the other track is moving ahead, the machine will

frames.name: p013-text-1123
frames.text: be turned in the narrowest possible radius. The radius in which

frames.name: p013-text-1124
frames.text: the machine can be turned depends to a large extent upon the nature

frames.name: p013-text-1125
frames.text: of the ground, as owing to its weight, it will dig up the ground to

frames.name: p013-text-1126
frames.text: the side as it is being turned, which will impede the rate at which

frames.name: p013-text-1127
frames.text: it can be swung around and will sometimes necessitate a wider

frames.name: p013-text-1128
frames.text: turning arc.

frames.name: p013-text-1129
frames.text: PROGRESS OF DRIVE

frames.name: p013-text-1130
frames.text: The units employed in propelling the Mark VIII machine are the

frames.name: p013-text-1131
frames.text: engine, which is the source of power; the clutch which connects

frames.name: p013-text-1132
frames.text: the source of power with the reduction gearing; an epicyclic or

frames.name: p013-text-1133
frames.text: planetary gear box which contains the reduction gear; a chain drive

frames.name: p014-text-1150
frames.text: DRIVE AND CONTROL

frames.name: p014-text-1151
frames.text: Control of the engine, clutch, epicyclic gear, reduction, steering,

frames.name: p014-text-1152
frames.text: etc., are all taken care of from the driver’s seat, which is located in

frames.name: p014-text-1153
frames.text: the forward end of the hull. The driver’s seat is of such a height

frames.name: p014-text-1154
frames.text: that the driver’s head is within a boxlike structure at the front

frames.name: p014-text-1155
frames.text: end of the main turret. There are slits cut in this compartment

frames.name: p014-text-1156
frames.text: which allow the driver to look to either side or ahead. The slits

frames.name: p014-text-1157
frames.text: can be closed by rotating protecting shields when under fire, and

frames.name: p014-text-1158
frames.text: when not under fire, the driver can raise a hinged door at the front

frames.name: p014-text-1159
frames.text: of the turret, allowing a clear and unobstructed view ahead of the

frames.name: p014-text-1160
frames.text: machine.

frames.name: p014-text-1161
frames.text: Outside of the spark and throttle connections and other engine

frames.name: p014-text-1162
frames.text: controls, the driver has four levers and a peddle. The two inside

frames.name: p014-text-1163
frames.text: levers are for shifting gears and control the epicyclic transmission.

frames.name: p014-text-1164
frames.text: The left outside lever controls the clutch and the right outside lever

frames.name: p014-text-1165
frames.text: is for reversing the peddle which is in the center of the track brake.

frames.name: p014-text-1166
frames.text: When either shifting lever is in neutral, the track brake on that aside

frames.name: p014-text-1167
frames.text: can be applied so that shifting both levers to neutral permits apply-

frames.name: p014-text-1168
frames.text: ing track brake to both tracks.

frames.name: p014-text-1169
frames.text: BRIEF OPERATING INSTRUCTIONS

frames.name: p014-text-1170
frames.text: PRELIMINARY TO STARTING ENGINE

frames.name: p014-text-1171
frames.text: Before running, thoroughly clean all parts coated with grease or

frames.name: p014-text-1172
frames.text: slush applied for protection in shipment.

frames.name: p014-text-1173
frames.text: Fill radiator and water tanks with clear water.

frames.name: p014-text-1174
frames.text: Fill engine-oil reservoir. (See page 51.)

frames.name: p014-text-1175
frames.text: Plate No. 5

frames.name: p014-text-1176
frames.text: THREE-QUARTER FRONT VIEW OF MARK VIII MACHINE

frames.name: p015-text-1178
frames.text: Fill oil reservoir of epicyclic transmission.

frames.name: p015-text-1179
frames.text: Lubricate entire machine in accordance with instructions. (See

frames.name: p015-text-1180
frames.text: pages 17 to 27.)

frames.name: p015-text-1181
frames.text: Unpack and place all tools and equipment in proper locations.

frames.name: p015-text-1182
frames.text: (See Nomenclature List, pages 184 to 239, and other parts of book

frames.name: p015-text-1183
frames.text: dealing with specific tools and equipment.)

frames.name: p015-text-1184
frames.text: Important Note.—Before attempting to drive the Mark VIII

frames.name: p015-text-1185
frames.text: machine, be certain that the brake on the cardan shift is adjusted,

frames.name: p015-text-1186
frames.text: so that in shifting, the spinning of the shaft will be stopped or serious

frames.name: p015-text-1187
frames.text: damage to the transmission will occur.

frames.name: p015-text-1188
frames.text: HOW TO DRIVE

frames.name: p015-text-1189
frames.text: To drive the machine, the following routine should be observed:

frames.name: p015-text-1190
frames.text: 1. Follow instructions on pages 51 to 61 regarding putting the

frames.name: p015-text-1191
frames.text: engine in condition to start.

frames.name: p015-text-1192
frames.text: 2. Make sure that reversing lever is in neutral and clutch in full

frames.name: p015-text-1193
frames.text: in position.

frames.name: p015-text-1194
frames.text: 3. Start engine as per directions on page 51.

frames.name: p015-text-1195
frames.text: 4. Allow engine to warm up so that the temperature of the cooling

frames.name: p015-text-1196
frames.text: water in radiator is at least 160 degrees.

frames.name: p015-text-1197
frames.text: 5. Make sure epicyclic levers are in neutral.

frames.name: p015-text-1198
frames.text: 6. Pull back clutch lever all the way.

frames.name: p015-text-1199
frames.text: 7. Put reverse lever into forward position carefully and slowly.

frames.name: p015-text-1200
frames.text: 8. Let clutch in slowly.

frames.name: p015-text-1201
frames.text: 9. Let epicyclic lever into low speed (outside slots) and machine

frames.name: p015-text-1202
frames.text: will slowly start.

frames.name: p015-text-1203
frames.text: 10. Shift either left or right lever to high speed, leaving clutch

frames.name: p015-text-1204
frames.text: engaged. (See page 150.) This will cause machine to swing in a

frames.name: p015-text-1205
frames.text: long arc due to difference in speed of tracks, but it is an easy way of

frames.name: p015-text-1206
frames.text: taking up the increased load due to shifting into high gear.

frames.name: p015-text-1207
frames.text: 11. Shift other lever to high gear.

frames.name: p015-text-1208
frames.text: SHIFTING TO LOW

frames.name: p015-text-1209
frames.text: To shift to low gear it is only necessary to move the levers into

frames.name: p015-text-1210
frames.text: low gear position without touching clutch.

frames.name: p015-text-1211
frames.text: TO REVERSE MACHINE

frames.name: p015-text-1212
frames.text: 1. Put both shifting levers in neutral.

frames.name: p015-text-1213
frames.text: 2. Pull clutch lever back as far as it will go.

frames.name: p015-text-1214
frames.text: 3. When sure that cardan shift has stopped running, shift to reverse

frames.name: p015-text-1215
frames.text: by putting reverse lever in position (as shown on page 151).

frames.name: p015-text-1216
frames.text: 4. Engage both low gears.

frames.name: p015-text-1217
frames.text: 5. Let clutch in gradually.

frames.name: p015-text-1218
frames.text: TO STEER MACHINE

frames.name: p015-text-1219
frames.text: To turn, put track on side toward which it is desired to turn into

frames.name: p015-text-1220
frames.text: neutral. If machine does not turn quickly, but moves ahead, de-

frames.name: p015-text-1221
frames.text: press foot pedal.

frames.name: p015-text-1222
frames.text: The pedal brake is interconnected with the transmission, so that

frames.name: p015-text-1223
frames.text: the brake can only be applied on the side which is in neutral.

frames.name: p016-text-1225
frames.text: The pedal is a positive brake on the track which is in neutral; it

frames.name: p016-text-1226
frames.text: does not effect a track when it is in low or high gear. Placing the

frames.name: p016-text-1227
frames.text: lever in neutral allows the brake on that side to be applied when pres-

frames.name: p016-text-1228
frames.text: sure is applied to the pedal.

frames.name: p016-text-1229
frames.text: TO MAKE A WIDE TURN

frames.name: p016-text-1230
frames.text: To make a wide turn, the track on the side toward which it is

frames.name: p016-text-1231
frames.text: desired to turn should be in low gear, while the other track should

frames.name: p016-text-1232
frames.text: be in high gear. This allows the track on one side to turn at a faster

frames.name: p016-text-1233
frames.text: rate than that on the other and will give the wide turning arc desired.

frames.name: p016-text-1234
frames.text: PASSING OVER OBSTRUCTION

frames.name: p016-text-1235
frames.text: In going over all obstructions which are sufficiently high to lift the

frames.name: p016-text-1236
frames.text: front end of the machine clear of the ground, the speed levers should

frames.name: p016-text-1237
frames.text: be slipped to allow the machine to ease itself over the obstructions.

frames.name: p016-text-1238
frames.text: It will be remembered that the weight of this machine is about 40

frames.name: p016-text-1239
frames.text: tons and it has to be allowed to gently absorb the shock due to its

frames.name: p016-text-1240
frames.text: returning to normal position after having been lifted clear of the

frames.name: p016-text-1241
frames.text: ground. By allowing the speed levers to slip the machine will grad-

frames.name: p016-text-1242
frames.text: ually come back into contact with the ground and the jar and shock

frames.name: p016-text-1243
frames.text: which would otherwise result can be avoided.

frames.name: p016-text-1244

frames.name: p017-text-1247
frames.text: TRANSPORTING MARK VIII MACHINE

frames.name: p017-text-1248
frames.text: To accommodate the Mark VIII machine to the ordinary railway

frames.name: p017-text-1249
frames.text: transportation methods, it is possible to swing the sponsons in front

frames.name: p017-text-1250
frames.text: by the methods told on page 37. When the sponsons are swung in as

frames.name: p017-text-1251
frames.text: thus described and the guns in the sponsons are drawn back, the

frames.name: p017-text-1252
frames.text: standard railway flat car can be used.

frames.name: p017-text-1253
frames.text: MILEAGE PER GALLON OF GASOLINE

frames.name: p017-text-1254
frames.text: It is estimated that the machine will consume 30 gallons per hour

frames.name: p017-text-1255
frames.text: of travel. At the speed of 5 miles per hour, this would mean one-

frames.name: p017-text-1256
frames.text: sixth of a mile per gallon, or with a capacity of 240 gallons, this would

frames.name: p017-text-1257
frames.text: mean a cruising time of eight hours or a cruising range of about 40

frames.name: p017-text-1258
frames.text: miles, estimating that the machine consumes 6 gallons per mile.

frames.name: p017-text-1259
frames.text: This, however, is only an estimate, and will vary in practice.

frames.name: p017-text-1260
frames.text: LUBRICATING INSTRUCTIONS

frames.name: p017-text-1261
frames.text: The lubrication of the Mark VIII machine is highly important, and

frames.name: p017-text-1262
frames.text: the performance of the machine depends largely upon how well the

frames.name: p017-text-1263
frames.text: following instructions are carried out. They should be made a matter

frames.name: p017-text-1264
frames.text: of routine, and followed exactly as laid down herewith.

frames.name: p017-text-1265
frames.text: ENGINE LUBRICATION

frames.name: p017-text-1266
frames.text: The engine is lubricated from a reservoir on the starboard side of

frames.name: p017-text-1267
frames.text: the hull alongside the engine. Although the capacity of this tank

frames.name: p017-text-1268
frames.text: fitted on the machine is 16 gallons, not more than 4 or 5 gallons of

frames.name: p017-text-1269
frames.text: Plate No. 7

frames.name: p018-text-1271
frames.text: Liberty engine oil (see page 54) should be put in. If more than that

frames.name: p018-text-1272
frames.text: is put in, the tank is apt to flood the engine. This tank oils all parts

frames.name: p018-text-1273
frames.text: of the engine except one oil cup at the thrust bearing. This cup

frames.name: p018-text-1274
frames.text: should be filled daily.

frames.name: p018-text-1275
frames.text: LOWER ROAD TRACK ROLLERS

frames.name: p018-text-1276
frames.text: The lower road track rollers are lubricated by removing the plugs on

frames.name: p018-text-1277
frames.text: the ends of the roller shafts. These rollers should receive a squirt

frames.name: p018-text-1278
frames.text: from the oil can once or twice a week, and the oil used should

frames.name: p018-text-1279
frames.text: correspond to the well-known 600-W grade.

frames.name: p018-text-1280
frames.text: UPPER ROAD TRACK ROLLERS

frames.name: p018-text-1281
frames.text: The upper road track rollers are lubricated by removing the plugs

frames.name: p018-text-1282
frames.text: on the ends of the roller shafts, and filling as full as possible once or

frames.name: p018-text-1283
frames.text: twice a week with oil corresponding to the 600-W grade.

frames.name: p018-text-1284
frames.text: EPICYCLIC GEAR

frames.name: p018-text-1285
frames.text: Be sure that the cups on each side of the epicyclic gear case, into

frames.name: p018-text-1286
frames.text: which passes the lead for the main bearings, is kept full of wool waste.

frames.name: p018-text-1287
frames.text: This allows of the gradual feed to the main bearings. No other

frames.name: p018-text-1288
frames.text: packing material should be placed in these cups, as the results will

frames.name: p018-text-1289
frames.text: not be satisfactory.

frames.name: p018-text-1290
frames.text: The epicyclic gear is lubricated from the oil tank on the starboard

frames.name: p018-text-1291
frames.text: side of the hull, above the removable side plate. This oil tank is

frames.name: p018-text-1292
frames.text: filled through the plugs in the top, and has a capacity of 2 gallons of

frames.name: p018-text-1293
frames.text: 600-W oil. The tank should be inspected weekly, and filled to the

frames.name: p018-text-1294
frames.text: Plate No. 8

frames.name: p019-text-1296
frames.text: top. The oil is carried from the tank by a mechanical lubricator,

frames.name: p019-text-1297
frames.text: which oils the four main bearings, and the roller pinion shaft.

frames.name: p019-text-1298
frames.text: There is a cap on the top of the bevel gear case which should be

frames.name: p019-text-1299
frames.text: filled once a week, having a capacity of 2 gallons. This takes care

frames.name: p019-text-1300
frames.text: of the bevel gears and the shifter clutch, which governs the forward

frames.name: p019-text-1301
frames.text: and reverse speeds.

frames.name: p019-text-1302
frames.text: The epicylic gear trains are taken care of by removing the two

frames.name: p019-text-1303
frames.text: caps or plugs in the gear case, and filling once a week with 3 gallons

frames.name: p019-text-1304
frames.text: of oil. To flush out the gear case, which revolves, the cap is first

frames.name: p019-text-1305
frames.text: brought to the top, and the gear case filled with kerosene and then

frames.name: p019-text-1306
frames.text: allowed to rotate to the bottom for draining. The case can then be

frames.name: p019-text-1307
frames.text: brought back so that the cap is at the top, and can be refilled by

frames.name: p019-text-1308
frames.text: putting 3 gallons of oil in each of the oil holes.

frames.name: p019-text-1309
frames.text: FRONT CONTROL RODS

frames.name: p019-text-1310
frames.text: The front control rods are lubricated through the oil holes in the

frames.name: p019-text-1311
frames.text: lever shaft. Each of these holes should be given a squirt from the

frames.name: p019-text-1312
frames.text: oil can at least once a month.

frames.name: p019-text-1313
frames.text: Plate No. 9

frames.name: p020-text-1317
frames.text: To lubricate the center control rods it is necessary to remove the

frames.name: p020-text-1318
frames.text: center section of the ammunition rack. This can be lifted out, as

frames.name: p020-text-1319
frames.text: it is separated from the rack itself. The lubrication of the center

frames.name: p021-text-0002
frames.text: control rods is taken care of by oil holes on the top of each unit, and

frames.name: p021-text-0003

frames.text: REAR CONTROL RODS

frames.name: p022-text-0010
frames.text: The rear control rods should receive a drop of oil weekly on the

frames.name: p022-text-0011
frames.text: pins and on the wearing points.

frames.name: p022-text-0012
frames.text: TRACK LINK PINS

frames.name: p022-text-0013
frames.text: The pins which connect the track links should receive an oil bath

frames.name: p022-text-0014
frames.text: in assembly. The track should be run through an oil bath monthly

frames.name: p022-text-0015
frames.text: by driving the machine through a prepared oil pool, or by swabbing

frames.name: p022-text-0016
frames.text: at accessible points, such as the mudholes.

frames.name: p022-text-0017
frames.text: COOLING FAN

frames.name: p022-text-0018
frames.text: The Sirocco cooling fan is lubricated through the oil plugs. There

frames.name: p022-text-0019
frames.text: is one plug on the fan casing and the other plug on the fan shaft.

frames.name: p022-text-0020
frames.text: These should receive a squirt from the oil can weekly.

frames.name: p022-text-0021
frames.text: VENTILATING FANS

frames.name: p022-text-0022
frames.text: The ventilating fan is lubricated by removing the oil plugs on the

frames.name: p022-text-0023
frames.text: ventilating-fan casing. Each of these holes should receive a squirt

frames.name: p022-text-0024
frames.text: from the oil can weekly.

frames.name: p022-text-0025
frames.text: Plate No. 14

frames.name: p022-text-0026
frames.text: FAN BEVEL BOX

frames.name: p023-text-0028
frames.text: ROAD TRACK DRIVING WHEEL

frames.name: p023-text-0029
frames.text: The road track driving wheel is lubricated by removable plates on

frames.name: p023-text-0030
frames.text: the ends of the ventilating-fan driving-wheel shafts. They are on

frames.name: p023-text-0031
frames.text: the outside of the machine. The oil can should be applied to put as

frames.name: p023-text-0032
frames.text: much oil of the equivalent of 600-W as possible into the boss. This

frames.name: p023-text-0033
frames.text: should be done weekly.

frames.name: p023-text-0034
frames.text: ROAD TRACK ADJUSTING WHEEL

frames.name: p023-text-0035
frames.text: The road track adjusting wheel is oiled through the plugs on the

frames.name: p023-text-0036
frames.text: ends of the road track adjusting-wheel shafts. The plugs are re-

frames.name: p023-text-0037
frames.text: moved, and by means of a squirt can as much 600-W oil as possible is

frames.name: p023-text-0038
frames.text: introduced. This should be done weekly.

frames.name: p023-text-0039
frames.text: ROAD TRACK ADJUSTING SCREW

frames.name: p023-text-0040
frames.text: Before attempting to adjust the track the threads of the road track

frames.name: p023-text-0041
frames.text: adjusting screw should be cleaned and thoroughly oiled. This

frames.name: p023-text-0042
frames.text: should be done whenever the track is adjusted.

frames.name: p023-text-0043
frames.text: Plate No. 15

frames.name: p023-text-0044
frames.text: AIR PUMP

frames.name: p024-text-0046
frames.text: DRIVE CHAIN

frames.name: p024-text-0047
frames.text: The sprocket drive chain should be lubricated through the holes in

frames.name: p024-text-0048
frames.text: the links. It should also be well lubricated before assembly. This

frames.name: p024-text-0049
frames.text: should be taken care of daily if the machine is in service.

frames.name: p024-text-0050
frames.text: ROLLER PINIONS

frames.name: p024-text-0051
frames.text: The roller pinions are lubricated through the holes in their cir-

frames.name: p024-text-0052
frames.text: cumference. To reach this remove the end hull plate on the side.

frames.name: p024-text-0053
frames.text: This should receive a squirt of oil monthly.

frames.name: p024-text-0054
frames.text: CLUTCH-CONTROL SHAFT

frames.name: p024-text-0055
frames.text: The clutch has a shaft which holds the clutch-control links. The

frames.name: p024-text-0056
frames.text: oil holes in the links should receive a squirt from the oil can weekly.

frames.name: p024-text-0057
frames.text: AIR PUMP

frames.name: p024-text-0058
frames.text: The air pump should receive oil through the two plugs in the top of

frames.name: p024-text-0059
frames.text: the pump. About a cup full of oil is required for each of these plugs,

frames.name: p024-text-0060
frames.text: and they should be lubricated weekly.

frames.name: p024-text-0061
frames.text: FAN BEVEL BOX

frames.name: p024-text-0062
frames.text: The fan bevel box should contain about a quart of 600-W oil, or

frames.name: p024-text-0063
frames.text: equivalent, and should be filled monthly.

frames.name: p024-text-0064
frames.text: Plate No. 16

frames.name: p025-text-0066
frames.text: JOCKEY PULLEY

frames.name: p025-text-0067
frames.text: The jockey pulley is lubricated through the plug in the side of the

frames.name: p025-text-0068
frames.text: pulley, opposite the ball-bearing center. This should receive a squirt

frames.name: p025-text-0069
frames.text: from the oil can every week.

frames.name: p025-text-0070
frames.text: GENERATOR

frames.name: p025-text-0071
frames.text: The generator has two oil plugs on the side, into each of which two

frames.name: p025-text-0072
frames.text: or three drops of light oil, such as Veedol light, should be placed,

frames.name: p025-text-0073
frames.text: biweekly.

frames.name: p025-text-0074
frames.text: STARTING MOTOR

frames.name: p025-text-0075
frames.text: There are two oil plugs on each end of the starting motor, into

frames.name: p025-text-0076
frames.text: which two or three drops of light Veedol oil should be placed, bi-

frames.name: p025-text-0077
frames.text: weekly.

frames.name: p025-text-0078
frames.text: CLUTCH

frames.name: p025-text-0079
frames.text: All accessible bearing parts of the clutch, with the exception of the

frames.name: p025-text-0080
frames.text: cone surface, should receive a squirt of oil from the can weekly.

frames.name: p025-text-0081
frames.text: ROAD TRACK

frames.name: p025-text-0082
frames.text: Before placing the road track on the machine give the links a

frames.name: p025-text-0083
frames.text: thick coating of heavy oil, and also the drive-wheel teeth, in order to

frames.name: p025-text-0084
frames.text: reduce the wear on the links.

frames.name: p025-text-0085

frames.text: SPONSON HINGES

frames.name: p026-text-0089
frames.text: The sponson hinges and rollers should receive a few drops of oil

frames.name: p026-text-0090
frames.text: monthly, and before drawing in the sponson.

frames.text: The following parts should be lubricated biweekly: Lower road

frames.text: GENERAL DESCRIPTION

frames.name: p030-text-0180
frames.text: The gasoline or petrol supply is carried in three tanks, of 80 gallons

frames.name: p030-text-0181
frames.text: capacity each, mounted near the rear of the machine, just below the

frames.name: p030-text-0182
frames.text: top plating. The gasoline or petrol tanks are all similar, and are

frames.name: p030-text-0183
frames.text: mounted side by side. The gasoline is forced by pressure from these

frames.name: p030-text-0184
frames.text: three tanks to a gravity tank mounted directly above the engine,

frames.name: p030-text-0185
frames.text: from which the flow is by gravity and pressure to the two carburetors.

frames.name: p030-text-0186
frames.text: Pressure is supplied by the engine-driven air pump, the pump being

frames.name: p031-text-0230
frames.text: THE AIR-PUMP DRIVE

frames.name: p031-text-0231
frames.text: The air pump is mounted just above the clutch, and is driven by a

frames.name: p031-text-0232
frames.text: V belt on the pulley on the engine-shaft brake. The pulley on the

frames.name: p031-text-0233
frames.text: air pump operates the cam shaft, which works directly against the

frames.name: p031-text-0234
frames.text: pistons or plungers of the pump. Before the engine is in motion, a

frames.name: p031-text-0235
frames.text: sufficient pressure can be secured to start the flow of fuel by means

frames.name: p031-text-0236
frames.text: of a hand pump, located on the bulkhead between the engine room

frames.name: p031-text-0237
frames.text: and fighting compartment. The flow is received from one of these

frames.name: p031-text-0238
frames.text: three tanks, depending upon which one of the cocks is open to the

frames.name: p031-text-0239
frames.text: gravity tank, located above the engine. The triple combination tap

frames.name: p031-text-0240
frames.text: is a ground key cock type, with a T handle between the tank and

frames.name: p031-text-0241
frames.text: carburetor, and controls the flow from the individual tanks. The

frames.name: p031-text-0242
frames.text: type of connections used on the gasoline system are flexible metal

frames.name: p031-text-0243
frames.text: hose soldered into T union connections.

frames.name: p031-text-0244
frames.text: TO FILL GASOLINE SYSTEM

frames.name: p031-text-0245
frames.text: To fill the gasoline tank it is necessary to unlock the hinge plates

frames.name: p031-text-0246
frames.text: over the caps by means of a socket wrench key. These two hinged

frames.name: p031-text-0247
frames.text: plates are lifted up, and this exposes the three filler caps or inlets in

frames.name: p031-text-0248
frames.text: the top of the tank. These caps are removed, and the gasoline tanks

frames.name: p031-text-0249
frames.text: can be filled.

frames.name: p031-text-0250

frames.name: p031-text-0251

frames.text: AIR-PRESSURE SYSTEM

frames.name: p032-text-0272
frames.text: The gasoline system has a pressure feed (see p. 28) with three

frames.name: p032-text-0273
frames.text: supply tanks in the rear end of the hull and a pressure regulating

frames.name: p032-text-0274
frames.text: tank over the engine. The air pressure is furnished by a piston air

frames.name: p032-text-0275
frames.text: pump, mounted on a frame over the cardan shaft, from which the

frames.name: p032-text-0276
frames.text: pump is operated by means of a belt. Three air tubes of ¼-inch

frames.name: p032-text-0277
frames.text: armored flexible brass tubing run from the pump to the roof of the

frames.name: p032-text-0278
frames.text: machine, where they are connected to tees from one end of which

frames.name: p032-text-0279
frames.text: tubing of the same type leads along the under side of the roof to ball

frames.name: p032-text-0280
frames.text: check valves which are connected to the lower valves of the com-

frames.name: p032-text-0281
frames.text: bination tap which passes through the bulkhead between the engine

frames.name: p032-text-0282
frames.text: room and gasoline-tank compartment. From the rear end of the

frames.name: p032-text-0283
frames.text: combination tap ½-inch tubes lead to the top of the three gasoline

frames.name: p032-text-0284
frames.text: tanks.

frames.name: p032-text-0285
frames.text: From the forward ends of the tees ¼-inch outside diameter seam-

frames.name: p032-text-0286
frames.text: less copper tubing runs along the upper right-hand corner of the tank

frames.name: p032-text-0287
frames.text: to the bulkhead, where each is connected to a main tube of the same

frames.name: p032-text-0288
frames.text: which leads to a pressure hand pump mounted on the engine-room

frames.name: p032-text-0289
frames.text: bulkhead over the port engine-room door. On the engine-room bulk-

frames.name: p032-text-0290
frames.text: head are mounted air-pressure gauges, tubes from which are con-

frames.name: p032-text-0291
frames.text: nected with the tubes from the tanks to the hand pump. Between

frames.name: p032-text-0292
frames.text: the gauges and the main line to the pump are fitted ground spindle

frames.name: p032-text-0293
frames.text: valves with levers. From the remaining plug on the air-pressure

frames.name: p032-text-0294
frames.text: pump a ¼-inch flexible brass tube leads to the pressure-regulating

frames.name: p032-text-0295
frames.text: tank over the engine. Just before reaching the regulating tank it is

frames.name: p032-text-0296
frames.text: connected to a cross. From one side leads a ¼-inch copper tubing

frames.name: p032-text-0297
frames.text: which connects to a pressure gauge on the bulkhead showing the

frames.name: p032-text-0298
frames.text: pressure in the regulation tank. A pet cock is connected with the

frames.name: p032-text-0299
frames.text: other side of the tee.

frames.text: in H form, the cross bar of the H being the hull or body proper,

frames.name: p036-text-0450
frames.text: containing the engine and fighting compartments, while the uprights

frames.name: p036-text-0451
frames.text: of the H represent the side plates of the hull which also act as guides

frames.name: p036-text-0452
frames.text: for the track.

frames.name: p036-text-0453
frames.text: Not only does the hull act as the container or housing for the

frames.name: p036-text-0454
frames.text: driving and fighting mechanism as well as the crew, but it is also the

frames.name: p036-text-0455
frames.text: backbone structure of the entire machine. The plating of the hull,

frames.name: p036-text-0456
frames.text: therefore, performs the three functions of acting as a housing, as a

frames.name: p036-text-0457
frames.text: protection and also as a supporting structure.

frames.text: REAR END SHOWING TRIANGULAR SPLASH PLATE AND TOWING EYE

frames.name: p037-text-0461
frames.text: Within the sides of the hull and projecting from it are two sponsons

frames.name: p037-text-0462
frames.text: which carry 6-pounder guns. These sponsons are carried outboard to

frames.name: p037-text-0463
frames.text: allow the guns to have a forward range as well as covering a wide arc

frames.name: p037-text-0464
frames.text: on either side of the machine. They are located at the forward end

frames.name: p037-text-0465
frames.text: of the fighting compartment. The gun mounts are capable of ro-

frames.name: p037-text-0466
frames.text: tating in the sponsons to give the necessary flexibility of fire.

frames.name: p037-text-0467
frames.text: In order to accomodate the Mark VIII machine to the limitations

frames.name: p037-text-0468
frames.text: of railway transportation it is possible to draw the sponsons inboard.

frames.name: p037-text-0469
frames.text: Plate No. 28

frames.name: p037-text-0470
frames.text: DOOR OF HULL SHOWING FITTINGS

frames.name: p038-text-0472
frames.text: This is accomplished by removing the bolts connecting the angle

frames.name: p038-text-0473
frames.text: bar flange with the hull shell plating at the rear end of the sponson.

frames.name: p038-text-0474
frames.text: Removing these bolts frees the sponson and allows it to be swung

frames.name: p038-text-0475
frames.text: back on a hinge bracketed to the forward extremity of the sponson

frames.name: p038-text-0476
frames.text: and to the shell plating at this point.

frames.name: p038-text-0477
frames.text: To further narrow the machine so that no part will project in ship-

frames.name: p038-text-0478
frames.text: ment by rail, beyond the 9-foot railway loading gauge, the guns in

frames.name: p038-text-0479
frames.text: the sponsons are drawn back. The machine-gun mounts which pro-

frames.name: p038-text-0480
frames.text: ject from the doors in the sides of the hull are also designed to just

frames.name: p038-text-0481
frames.text: equal, but not to exceed the 9-foot loading width.

frames.name: p038-text-0482
frames.text: SPONSON ROLLER

frames.name: p038-text-0483
frames.text: Near the inner edge of the sponson in rear of the ammunition stow-

frames.name: p038-text-0484
frames.text: age is the sponson roller which carried the weight of the sponson

frames.name: p038-text-0485
frames.text: when being moved in or out.

frames.name: p038-text-0486
frames.text: The sponson roller bracket is bolted to the floor of the sponson

frames.name: p038-text-0487
frames.text: above the floor plate, and has a short bearing on each side for the

frames.name: p038-text-0488
frames.text: roller shaft. The roller is 40 mm. bore, 110 mm. outside diameter

frames.name: p038-text-0489
frames.text: and 27 mm. wide and runs on roller track for the sponson, which is

frames.name: p038-text-0490
frames.text: on an arc of a circle with the sponson hinges as a center. The track

frames.name: p038-text-0491
frames.text: is a steel bar ¾ inch wide by 4 inches high and is held by bolts to

frames.name: p038-text-0492
frames.text: three brackets which are riveted to the floor.

frames.name: p038-text-0493
frames.text: MAIN TURRET

frames.name: p038-text-0494
frames.text: On the top of the hull there is located the main turret. This is

frames.name: p038-text-0495
frames.text: rectangular in form and carries surmounted upon it the lookout

frames.name: p038-text-0496
frames.text: turret which is also rectangular in form. At the forward end of the

frames.name: p038-text-0497
frames.text: main turret is located the driver’s turret, also of rectangular form.

frames.name: p038-text-0498
frames.text: The lookout turret is of such a height that when a man stands on the

frames.name: p038-text-0499
frames.text: officers’ kit box located on the ammunition storage compartment

frames.name: p038-text-0500
frames.text: below it, his head will be at the proper height to look out through

frames.name: p038-text-0501
frames.text: the peepholes on all sides of the machine.

frames.name: p038-text-0502
frames.text: Plate No. 29

frames.name: p039-text-0505
frames.text: HULL DOORS

frames.name: p039-text-0506
frames.text: There are three main doors in the hull; two are in the fighting com-

frames.name: p039-text-0507
frames.text: partment, located on each side at the rear, and the other is at the top

frames.name: p039-text-0508
frames.text: of the machine entering into the main turret from above. The side

frames.name: p039-text-0509
frames.text: doors are 28½ inches wide and 41⅞ inches high. The top door is 20

frames.name: p039-text-0510
frames.text: inches along the length of the machine and 15⅞ inches wide. In

frames.name: p039-text-0511
frames.text: addition, there are other openings in the hull for observation or other

frames.name: p039-text-0512
frames.text: purposes. In the front end of the driver’s turret there is a plate

frames.name: p039-text-0513
frames.text: which can be swung outward, allowing the driver a clear vision for-

frames.name: p039-text-0514
frames.text: ward when not under heavy fire. Similarly there are openings on

frames.name: p039-text-0515
frames.text: each side of the main turret just forward of the lookout turret which

frames.name: p039-text-0516
frames.text: can be swung open to give a clear view on either side of the machine.

frames.name: p039-text-0517
frames.text: The side doors leading into the fighting compartment are pierced for

frames.name: p039-text-0518
frames.text: machine-gun mounts and there are also five holes in the main turret to

frames.name: p039-text-0519
frames.text: provide for five additional machine guns. The spherical mounts for

frames.name: p039-text-0520
frames.text: these machine guns fit into these holes.

frames.text: LOUVERS

frames.name: p040-text-0561
frames.text: The top of the hull is pierced at the rear end between the tracks

frames.name: p040-text-0562
frames.text: by openings for the intake and exhaust air louvers. These louvers

frames.name: p040-text-0563
frames.text: are above the engine-room compartment. The intake louver is

frames.name: p040-text-0564
frames.text: above the forward end of the engine at the front end of the engine

frames.name: p040-text-0565
frames.text: compartment and the exhaust louver is above the radiator at the rear

frames.name: p040-text-0566
frames.text: end of the engine compartment. The openings in which the louvers

frames.name: p040-text-0567
frames.text: are fitted are rectangular. The dimensions of the intake-louver

frames.name: p040-text-0568
frames.text: opening are 3 feet 1¼ inches wide by 2 feet 1.825 inches long and the

frames.name: p040-text-0569
frames.text: exhaust-louver opening is 3 feet 1¼ inches wide by 3 feet 1⅝ inches

frames.name: p040-text-0570
frames.text: long.

frames.name: p040-text-0571
frames.text: The louvers are composed of bars of 6 mm. armor plate bent to an

frames.name: p040-text-0572
frames.text: angle of 90 degrees and spaced face to face in herringbone style,

frames.name: p040-text-0573
frames.text: so that while permitting the air to readily pass through they act as

frames.name: p040-text-0574
frames.text: a baffle against projectiles or fragments, causing them to lose their

frames.name: p040-text-0575
frames.text: energy before entering the engine compartment. The extreme width

frames.name: p040-text-0576
frames.text: of each louver blade, outside to outside, is 2½ inches. The radius

frames.name: p040-text-0577
frames.text: around which the blade is bent in turning to the 90-degree angle is

frames.name: p040-text-0578
frames.text: one-half inch. There are 29 blades in the outlet louver and 34 blades

frames.name: p040-text-0579
frames.text: in the inlet. The proper distance between the louvers is held by

frames.name: p040-text-0580
frames.text: 122 carbon steel distance pieces, which take care of both the inlet

frames.name: p040-text-0581
frames.text: and outlet louvers.

frames.name: p040-text-0582
frames.text: Plate No. 31

frames.name: p040-text-0583
frames.text: SIDE OF TURRET SHOWING CAMOUFLAGE BRACKET

frames.name: p041-text-0002
frames.text: As a further protection the louvers are set between two 6 mm.

frames.name: p041-text-0003
frames.text: flanged steel bars, projecting 8¾ inches above the top surface of the

frames.name: p041-text-0004
frames.text: hull, on each side of the louver.

frames.name: p041-text-0005
frames.text: TO REMOVE LOUVERS

frames.name: p041-text-0006
frames.text: To remove the louvers, pass a rope sling beneath the blades so as

frames.name: p041-text-0007
frames.text: to sustain them, then release the set screws on the end which jam the

frames.name: p041-text-0008
frames.text: assembly together. This will allow the entire unit to drop apart.

frames.name: p041-text-0009
frames.text: In shipping the Mark VIII tank the sponsons are swung inboard

frames.name: p041-text-0010
frames.text: and the observation tower lowered flush with the top of the main

frames.name: p041-text-0011
frames.text: turret.

frames.name: p042-text-0034
frames.text: TO REMOVE SPONSONS

frames.name: p042-text-0035
frames.text: To remove the sponsons, take out the pins from the hinges upon

frames.name: p042-text-0036
frames.text: which the sponsons swing inboard; then remove the bolts from the

frames.name: p042-text-0037
frames.text: rear of the sponsons which bolt them against the shell plating. The

frames.name: p042-text-0038
frames.text: 6-pounder guns should be removed from the sponsons (see p. 174),

frames.name: p042-text-0039
frames.text: as well as all other parts stored therein, before pulling the hinge pins

frames.name: p042-text-0040
frames.text: or removing the bolts. This should not be attempted without a

frames.name: p042-text-0041
frames.text: chain fall.

frames.name: p042-text-0042
frames.text: TO REPLACE SPONSONS

frames.name: p042-text-0043
frames.text: To assemble the sponson in place it should be lifted into its with-

frames.name: p042-text-0044
frames.text: drawn position by means of a chain fall or some other means and the

frames.name: p042-text-0045
frames.text: hinge pins then slipped into place. The nuts are placed on the hinge

frames.name: p042-text-0046
frames.text: pins and the sponson then swung into the outboard position, when

frames.name: p042-text-0047
frames.text: the bolts holding it to the shell plating can be fitted. If it is desired

frames.name: p042-text-0048
frames.text: to fully assemble the sponson the guns can be placed inboard before

frames.name: p042-text-0049
frames.text: the sponsons are fitted. If good lifting devices are handy the entire

frames.name: p042-text-0050
frames.text: unit can be assembled before it is lifted into position.

frames.name: p042-text-0051
frames.text: TO OPEN BULKHEAD DOOR

frames.name: p042-text-0052
frames.text: The bulkhead center door slides upward and downward in grooves

frames.name: p042-text-0053
frames.text: and can be held up by a hook on the bulkhead just over the opening,

frames.name: p042-text-0054
frames.text: the hook engaging in the handle of the door. The two side doors are

frames.name: p042-text-0055
frames.text: carried by two rollers, each running on a track over the doors, the

frames.name: p042-text-0056
frames.text: lower end being guided by a groove in the lower bulkhead plate.

frames.name: p042-text-0057
frames.text: The door is locked in the closed position by a lock catch engaging

frames.name: p042-text-0058
frames.text: against the bulkhead. The lock hand has a spring which keeps the

frames.name: p042-text-0059
frames.text: catch clear of the bulkhead when the door is open. To lock, push

frames.name: p042-text-0060
frames.text: the lock handle in, depressing the spring and turn the handle toward

frames.name: p042-text-0061
frames.text: the center of the bulkhead until the handle is locked.

frames.name: p042-text-0062
frames.text: MOUNTED ON BULKHEAD

frames.name: p042-text-0063
frames.text: The following parts are mounted on the bulkhead, between the

frames.name: p042-text-0064
frames.text: engine room and the fighting compartment:

frames.name: p042-text-0065
frames.text: The machine-gun ammunition racks at the top.

frames.name: p042-text-0066
frames.text: First-aid carrier at one end of the rack on the starboard side of the

frames.name: p042-text-0067
frames.text: bulkhead.

frames.name: p042-text-0068
frames.text: Machine-gun repair kit at the front end of the bulkhead.

frames.name: p042-text-0069
frames.text: Instrument board directly under the machine-gun rack, which

frames.name: p042-text-0070
frames.text: carries the oil gauge, three gasoline or petrol tank gauges, gasoline

frames.name: p042-text-0071
frames.text: gauge for auxiliary tank, tachometer, and yardometer.

frames.name: p042-text-0072
frames.text: To the right of the instrument board there is a pressure and a hand

frames.name: p042-text-0073
frames.text: pump, for supplying initial pressure to the gasoline or petrol tanks

frames.name: p042-text-0074
frames.text: and at the center near the floor is the starting crank. There are two

frames.name: p042-text-0075
frames.text: doors through the bulkhead, one on each side, leading into the engine

frames.name: p042-text-0076
frames.text: compartment.

frames.name: p045-text-0152
frames.text: GENERAL DESCRIPTION

frames.name: p045-text-0153
frames.text: The engine is mounted longitudinally within the hull of the machine

frames.name: p045-text-0154
frames.text: at the rear end. It is contained within the engine compartment,

frames.name: p045-text-0155
frames.text: inclosed by the two side walls of the hull, the floor, the upper plating

frames.name: p045-text-0156
frames.text: of the hull and the transverse bulkhead which separates the engine

frames.name: p045-text-0157
frames.text: compartment from the fighting compartment. It is a 12-cylinder

frames.name: p045-text-0158
frames.text: Liberty type, with singly cast cylinders and an overhead valve

frames.name: p045-text-0159
frames.text: action. The action is a V design, having six cylinders on each side,

frames.name: p045-text-0160
frames.text: and an independent cam shaft for each set of six cylinders. The

frames.name: p045-text-0161
frames.text: cam shaft is overhead, and each cam shaft operates directly on the

frames.name: p045-text-0162
frames.text: overhead rockers by means of roller followers. The valves open

frames.name: p045-text-0163
frames.text: downward into the cylinders. Each cam shaft has 24 cams, and

frames.name: p045-text-0164
frames.text: each is driven by a set of bevel gears from the cam shaft.

frames.name: p046-text-0261
frames.text: PREPARING ENGINE FOR SERVICE

frames.name: p046-text-0262
frames.text: While every possible precaution is taken at the factory to insure

frames.name: p046-text-0263
frames.text: Liberty engines being properly assembled, the human element,

frames.name: p046-text-0264
frames.text: which is not infallible, must always be considered; therefore:

frames.name: p046-text-0265
frames.text: 1. Inspect all visible bolts and nuts and see that they are properly

frames.name: p046-text-0266
frames.text: drawn up and securely locked.

frames.name: p046-text-0267
frames.text: 2. Inspect throttle and spark controls and see that throttles of

frames.name: p046-text-0268
frames.text: both carburetor assemblies are synchronized. See that throttle

frames.name: p046-text-0269
frames.text: control at driver’s seat permits full throttle opening.

frames.name: p046-text-0270
frames.text: See that spark control at driver’s seat permits the specified range

frames.name: p046-text-0271
frames.text: of advance and retard at the distributor. (10 degrees after dead

frames.name: p046-text-0272
frames.text: center retarded and 30 degrees before dead center advanced).

frames.name: p046-text-0273
frames.text: 3. Check tappet gap. With the cylinder set on the firing point

frames.name: p046-text-0274
frames.text: the gap between the inlet-valve tappets and the valve stems should

frames.name: p046-text-0275
frames.text: be 0.014 to 0.16 and between the exhaust-valve tappets and valve

frames.name: p046-text-0276
frames.text: stems should be 0.019 and 0.021.

frames.name: p046-text-0277
frames.text: 4. Inspect all electrical connections. See that all wire terminals

frames.name: p046-text-0278
frames.text: are properly soldered clean and firmly attached at the distributors,

frames.name: p046-text-0279
frames.text: generator, battery, switch, and voltage regulator.

frames.name: p046-text-0280
frames.text: All wire terminal nuts should be cotter pinned or screwed down on

frames.name: p046-text-0281
frames.text: lock washers.

frames.name: p046-text-0282
frames.text: See that all wires are properly insulated and supported at close

frames.name: p046-text-0283
frames.text: intervals in such a manner that the insulation will not be abraded.

frames.name: p046-text-0284
frames.text: 5. Inspect ignition system. Note whether or not the mark on the

frames.name: p046-text-0285
frames.text: distributor assembly base coincides with the corresponding mark on

frames.name: p046-text-0286
frames.text: the cam-shaft housing flange.

frames.name: p046-text-0287
frames.text: 6. Check each breaker individually by turning engine over until

frames.name: p046-text-0288
frames.text: breaker is wide open and testing “gap” (width of opening) by means

frames.name: p046-text-0289
frames.text: of thickness gauge marked “distributor contacts” attached to dis-

frames.name: p046-text-0290
frames.text: tributor wrench. Gap should be 0.010 to 0.013 of an inch.

frames.name: p046-text-0291
frames.text: 7. Check timing of one main breaker on each distributor assembly

frames.name: p046-text-0292
frames.text: with an eight-volt lamp and battery or with an electric torch.

frames.name: p046-text-0293
frames.text: 8. Check synchronization of two distributor assemblies.

frames.name: p046-text-0294
frames.text: Clean inside of distributor covers by wiping with soft cloth moist-

frames.name: p046-text-0295
frames.text: ened with alcohol or gasoline; dry carefully.

frames.name: p046-text-0296
frames.text: 9. Replace covers so that terminal marker 1 L is just to the left of

frames.name: p046-text-0297
frames.text: the red mark on the assembly bases spark retarded. With the engine

frames.name: p046-text-0298
frames.text: set on the firing point of No. 1 L cylinder—in other words, with the

frames.name: p046-text-0299
frames.text: No. 1 crank set 10 degrees past the compression dead center—the

frames.name: p046-text-0300
frames.text: carbon brush in the end of the distributor rotor should bear on the

frames.name: p046-text-0301
frames.text: brass contact marked 1 L on the distributor head.

frames.name: p047-text-0303
frames.text: 10. Remove spark plugs and inspect carefully for defective or

frames.name: p047-text-0304
frames.text: broken porcelain. The electrode should be tight in the insulator and

frames.name: p047-text-0305
frames.text: the insulator should be properly gasketed and drawn up tightly to

frames.name: p047-text-0306
frames.text: prevent gas leakage. Hot gas blowing through a plug will overheat

frames.name: p047-text-0307
frames.text: and render it inoperative. A spark plug which has been used and has

frames.name: p047-text-0308
frames.text: given satisfactory service is always safer than a new plug; therefore

frames.name: p047-text-0309
frames.text: do not discard spark plugs simply because they have been used, unless

frames.name: p047-text-0310
frames.text: it is known positively that they are defective.

frames.name: p047-text-0311
frames.text: Note.—Defects in spark plugs will be most apparent when the

frames.name: p047-text-0312
frames.text: plugs are hot.

frames.name: p047-text-0313
frames.text: 11. Check spark-plug gap should be 0.015 to 0.018 of an inch. A

frames.name: p047-text-0314
frames.text: gauge is provided marked “spark plug” on the distributor wrench.

frames.name: p047-text-0315
frames.text: 12. Clean plugs; use a stiff brush and gasoline.

frames.name: p047-text-0316
frames.text: 13. Replace plugs, being careful that gasket is in place and that

frames.name: p047-text-0317
frames.text: plug is drawn down tightly on it.

frames.name: p047-text-0318
frames.text: 14. Trace out high-tension wires from the distributors and be sure

frames.name: p047-text-0319
frames.text: that each plug is connected to the correspondingly marked terminal

frames.name: p047-text-0320
frames.text: on the distributor.

frames.name: p047-text-0321
frames.text: Note.—Plugs on the side of the cylinders toward the flywheel are

frames.name: p047-text-0322
frames.text: connected to the left-hand distributor. Plugs on the opposite side of

frames.name: p047-text-0323
frames.text: the cylinders are connected on the right-hand distributor.

frames.name: p047-text-0324
frames.text: Order of firing.—Standing at the distributor end of the engine and

frames.name: p047-text-0325
frames.text: looking toward the flywheel, the groups of cylinders are designated as

frames.name: p047-text-0326
frames.text: left and right, respectively, and are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6,

frames.name: p047-text-0327
frames.text: beginning at the distributor end. The order of firing is as follows:

frames.name: p047-text-0328
frames.text: THE GASOLINE SYSTEM

frames.name: p047-text-0329
frames.text: 15. Connect pipes, and, with gasoline shut-off cock open, inspect all

frames.name: p047-text-0330
frames.text: piping and connections carefully for leaks. Inspect gasoline strainer

frames.name: p047-text-0331
frames.text: for leaks.

frames.name: p047-text-0332
frames.text: Be sure that carburetor float chambers fill properly and that

frames.name: p047-text-0333
frames.text: carburetor does not “flood.” To determine whether or not the car-

frames.name: p047-text-0334
frames.text: buretor float chamber is full, unscrew the cap over the needle valve.

frames.name: p047-text-0335
frames.text: If the chamber is full the needle will be down on its seat and can not

frames.name: p047-text-0336
frames.text: be depressed further. If this needle can be pressed down it would

frames.name: p047-text-0337
frames.text: indicate either a stoppage in the pipe or insufficient pressure in the

frames.name: p047-text-0338
frames.text: tank.

frames.name: p047-text-0339
frames.text: 16. Close gasoline shut-off cock. Caution: If temperature is 40

frames.text: degrees Fahr. above zero or lower, follow “cold weather suggestions”

frames.text: 17. Examine the radiator, pump, water jackets, piping, and all

frames.text: 18. Fill engine-oiling system. Lubricating oil of the following

frames.name: p049-text-0404
frames.text: properties is recommended:

frames.name: p049-text-0405
frames.text: ENGINE-OIL SPECIFICATIONS

frames.name: p049-text-0406
frames.text: High specific gravity oils.—This class includes all oils having a

frames.name: p049-text-0407
frames.text: specific gravity above 0.9100 (or below 24° Baumé conversion by the

frames.name: p049-text-0408
frames.text: Tagliabue Manual, ninth edition, or below 23.85° Baumé conversion

frames.name: p049-text-0409
frames.text: by the Bureau of Standards’ conversion table, Circular No. 57) having

frames.name: p049-text-0410
frames.text: a pour test below 15° F. (Tested by the method of the American

frames.name: p049-text-0411
frames.text: Society for Testing Materials).

frames.name: p049-text-0412
frames.text: Low specific gravity oils.—This class includes all oils having a

frames.name: p049-text-0413
frames.text: specific gravity below 0.9100 (or above 24° Baumé conversion by the

frames.name: p049-text-0414
frames.text: Tagliabue Manual, ninth edition, or above 23.85° Baumé conversion

frames.name: p049-text-0415
frames.text: by the Bureau of Standards’ conversion table, Circular No. 57) and

frames.name: p049-text-0416
frames.text: having a pour test above 15° F. (Tested by the method of the

frames.name: p049-text-0417
frames.text: American Society for Testing Materials.)

frames.name: p049-text-0418
frames.text: Physical properties and tests.—The oil must be made from pure,

frames.name: p049-text-0419
frames.text: highly refined petroleum products, and must be suitable in every way

frames.name: p049-text-0420
frames.text: for the entire lubrication of stationary cylinder aircraft engines

frames.name: p049-text-0421
frames.text: operating under all conditions.

frames.name: p049-text-0422
frames.text: Viscosity.—The viscosity of the oil when tested in a Saybolt

frames.name: p049-text-0423
frames.text: Universal Viscosimeter at 212° F., shall be as follows:

frames.name: p049-text-0424
frames.text: High specific gravity oil, 70 seconds to 75 seconds.

frames.name: p049-text-0425
frames.text: Low specific gravity oil, 85 seconds to 90 seconds.

frames.name: p049-text-0426
frames.text: Pour test.—The oil must pass the following pour test:

frames.name: p049-text-0427
frames.text: High specific gravity oil, not over 15° F.

frames.name: p049-text-0428
frames.text: Low specific gravity oil, not over 40° F.

frames.name: p049-text-0429
frames.text: Flash point.—The oil must have a flash point over 350 degrees

frames.name: p049-text-0430
frames.text: Fahr. in a Cleveland open cup.

frames.name: p049-text-0431
frames.text: Carbon.—The oil must not show a carbon residue of over 1.5 per

frames.name: p049-text-0432
frames.text: cent by the Conradson method. The carbon shown must be loose

frames.name: p049-text-0433
frames.text: and flaky and must break up easily in the crucible.

frames.name: p049-text-0434
frames.text: Emulsion test.—One ounce of oil shall be placed in a standard 4-

frames.name: p049-text-0435
frames.text: ounce sample bottle with 1 ounce of distilled water. The mixture shall

frames.name: p049-text-0436
frames.text: be heated to a temperature of 180° F. and then shaken vigorously

frames.name: p049-text-0437
frames.text: for five minutes. After standing for one hour the oil must be clear

frames.name: p049-text-0438
frames.text: and of the same color as before the test. All the water must have

frames.name: p049-text-0439
frames.text: settled and appear only slightly cloudy.

frames.name: p049-text-0440
frames.text: All tests must be made in accordance with methods adopted by the

frames.name: p049-text-0441
frames.text: American Society for Testing Materials. Detailed descriptions of the

frames.name: p050-text-0443
frames.text: Plate No. 36

frames.name: p050-text-0444
frames.text: COOLING SYSTEM

frames.name: p051-text-0446
frames.text: Conradson Carbon Test and the Pour Test have been reprinted in

frames.name: p051-text-0447
frames.text: Signal Corps Specifications No. 3525, which will be furnished on

frames.name: p051-text-0448
frames.text: application.

frames.name: p051-text-0449
frames.text: Physical properties and tests to be determined as follows:

frames.name: p051-text-0450
frames.text: Gravity: Baumé, at 60° F.

frames.name: p051-text-0451
frames.text: Flash: Cleveland open cup.

frames.name: p051-text-0452
frames.text: Fire: Cleveland open cup.

frames.name: p051-text-0453
frames.text: Viscosity: Saybolt Universal Viscosimeter, at 100°, 130°, and 212°F.

frames.name: p051-text-0454
frames.text: Pour test: American Society for Testing Materials’ method.

frames.name: p051-text-0455
frames.text: Carbon: Conradson method.

frames.name: p051-text-0456
frames.text: Color: Lovibund.

frames.name: p051-text-0457
frames.text: FILLING ENGINE-OIL RESERVOIR

frames.name: p051-text-0458
frames.text: Remove plug on side of oil-pump housing during the process of

frames.name: p051-text-0459
frames.text: filling the reservoir and allow it to remain out until oil flows from it.

frames.name: p051-text-0460
frames.text: Do not fill reservoir more than three-quarters full.

frames.name: p051-text-0461
frames.text: 19. See that ignition switches are in “off” position and try com-

frames.name: p051-text-0462
frames.text: pression of each cylinder separately by cranking the engine over

frames.name: p051-text-0463
frames.text: slowly by means of the crank and “rocking” it up to each compres-

frames.name: p051-text-0464
frames.text: sion point. Any weak cylinders can readily be detected, either by

frames.name: p051-text-0465
frames.text: the decreased resistance to cranking or by the hissing sound due to

frames.name: p051-text-0466
frames.text: the leaking valve or spark plug.

frames.name: p051-text-0467
frames.text: Locate the weak cylinder in the following manner: Crank the

frames.name: p051-text-0468
frames.text: engine over again, meanwhile watching the number 6-L exhaust

frames.name: p051-text-0469
frames.text: valve. When this valve is wide open the piston in No. 1-L cylinder

frames.name: p051-text-0470
frames.text: will be coming up on its compression stroke and just before the valve

frames.name: p051-text-0471
frames.text: closes No. 1-L will have reached its point of highest compression or

frames.name: p051-text-0472
frames.text: top dead center.

frames.name: p051-text-0473
frames.text: Now start from this point and crank the engine slowly past each

frames.name: p051-text-0474
frames.text: compression period, at the same time calling off the numbers of the

frames.name: p051-text-0475
frames.text: cylinders in their order of firing until the weak one is reached. For

frames.name: p051-text-0476
frames.text: the causes of loss of compression see page 59. It sometimes happens

frames.name: p051-text-0477
frames.text: that an engine will show uneven compression when cold, but will be all

frames.name: p051-text-0478
frames.text: right at running temperature, so that it is not advisable to assume that

frames.name: p051-text-0479
frames.text: anything is radically wrong with it until it has been warmed up and

frames.name: p051-text-0480
frames.text: the compression tested again.

frames.name: p051-text-0481
frames.text: TO START ENGINE

frames.name: p051-text-0482
frames.text: Before starting a new engine, or one which has stood idle for some

frames.name: p051-text-0483
frames.text: length of time, it is advisable to inject a small quantity of lubricating

frames.name: p051-text-0484
frames.text: oil (about one-half ounce) through each priming cock. With the igni-

frames.name: p051-text-0485
frames.text: tion switches “off,” turn the engine over through five or six revolutions

frames.name: p051-text-0486
frames.text: to distribute the oil over the cylinder walls.

frames.name: p051-text-0487
frames.text: Set throttle just slightly open; in other words, at a point which will

frames.name: p051-text-0488
frames.text: run the engine at 600 to 800 r. p. m.

frames.name: p051-text-0489
frames.text: Set spark at fully retarded position.

frames.name: p052-text-0491
frames.text: Plate No. 37

frames.name: p052-text-0492
frames.text: VALVE AND PUMP DRIVE

frames.name: p053-text-0494
frames.text: The ignition system for Liberty engines is so designed as to abso-

frames.name: p053-text-0495
frames.text: lutely prevent the production of a spark when turned backward, nor

frames.name: p053-text-0496
frames.text: will the engine “kick back” if it should happen to “rock” after

frames.name: p053-text-0497
frames.text: cranking. However, it is essential that the spark be retarded when

frames.name: p053-text-0498
frames.text: cranking.

frames.name: p053-text-0499
frames.text: Prime engine by injecting a small quantity (fill priming cock twice)

frames.name: p053-text-0500
frames.text: of gasoline through each priming cock. In cold weather it will be

frames.name: p053-text-0501
frames.text: necessary to prime the engine a little more heavily than in warm

frames.name: p053-text-0502
frames.text: weather. It is better, however, to insufficiently prime it than to

frames.name: p053-text-0503
frames.text: prime it too heavily.

frames.name: p053-text-0504
frames.text: With the ignition switch still “off,” turn engine forward two revolu-

frames.name: p053-text-0505
frames.text: tions.

frames.name: p053-text-0506
frames.text: Turn one (either one) ignition switch “on,” and start engine by

frames.name: p053-text-0507
frames.text: means of the electric starter or hand crank.

frames.name: p053-text-0508
frames.text: The switch is so designed that with both switches turned “on” the

frames.name: p053-text-0509
frames.text: generator is connected in, which will result in a rather high rate of

frames.name: p053-text-0510
frames.text: discharge from the battery and possible difficulty in starting. Both

frames.name: p053-text-0511
frames.text: switches should be turned “on,” however, as soon as the engine is

frames.name: p053-text-0512
frames.text: running.

frames.name: p053-text-0513
frames.text: As soon as the engine is started advance the spark about one-half

frames.name: p053-text-0514
frames.text: way, leaving the throttle in approximately the starting position, and

frames.name: p053-text-0515
frames.text: allow the engine to run at idling speed (about 800 r. p. m.) for five to

frames.name: p053-text-0516
frames.text: ten minutes, or until it is thoroughly warmed up. At the same time

frames.name: p053-text-0517
frames.text: test crank case temperature with your hand. The crank case should

frames.name: p053-text-0518
frames.text: be warm by the time the temperature of the water has increased to

frames.name: p053-text-0520
frames.text: Accelerate and slow down the engine occasionally to throw the oil

frames.name: p053-text-0521
frames.text: up into the cylinders.

frames.name: p053-text-0522
frames.text: In extremely cold weather it is possible that the cooling water

frames.name: p053-text-0523
frames.text: might warm up more rapidly than the lubrication oil. In this case

frames.name: p053-text-0524
frames.text: it would be advisable to stop the engine for a few moments in order

frames.name: p053-text-0525
frames.text: to allow the heat from the cylinders to travel down to the crank case.

frames.name: p053-text-0526
frames.text: In the meantime—

frames.name: p053-text-0527
frames.text: Note the oil-gauge pressure. After about three minutes running at

frames.name: p053-text-0528
frames.text: 600 to 800 r. p. m. this should show above 5 pounds pressure, and at

frames.name: p053-text-0529
frames.text: 1,600 r. p. m. up to 30 pounds maximum. Failure to show these

frames.name: p053-text-0530
frames.text: pressures may be due to dirt on the relief valve seat. The gauge

frames.name: p053-text-0531
frames.text: will show higher pressures when the engine is first started, and is

frames.name: p053-text-0532
frames.text: colder than after it has thoroughly warmed up.

frames.name: p053-text-0533
frames.text: Examine all oil piping for leaks.

frames.name: p053-text-0534
frames.text: AIR-PRESSURE GAUGE

frames.name: p053-text-0535
frames.text: Note air-pressure gauge.—The engine-driven air pump, with its regu-

frames.name: p053-text-0536
frames.text: lator, is designed to hold the pressure on the gasoline tank at approxi-

frames.name: p053-text-0537
frames.text: mately 3 pounds. In order to determine whether or not the pump

frames.name: p054-text-0538
frames.text: ENGINE-OIL SYSTEM

frames.name: p055-text-0541
frames.text: is functioning properly, screw down the pressure regulator adjusting

frames.name: p055-text-0542
frames.text: screw. This should cause the pressure in the tank to rise if the pump

frames.name: p055-text-0543
frames.text: is operating as it should. Now screw the regulator adjustment up

frames.name: p055-text-0544
frames.text: until the pressure is held steadily at 3 to 4 pounds.

frames.name: p055-text-0545
frames.text: Note water circulation.—Temperature gauge should show a steady

frames.name: p055-text-0546
frames.text: rise up to not to exceed 200° F. The most efficient temperature

frames.name: p055-text-0547
frames.text: will vary with weather conditions, but will average 180° F.

frames.name: p055-text-0548
frames.text: Note ammeter reading.—At idling speeds the ammeter needle will

frames.name: p055-text-0549
frames.text: stand on the “discharge” side of zero. At about 650 r. p. m., with

frames.name: p055-text-0550
frames.text: both switches “on,” the needle will stand at zero, and at high speeds

frames.name: p055-text-0551
frames.text: it should stand on the “charge” side of zero.

frames.name: p055-text-0552
frames.text: When the engine is well warmed up the throttle may be opened

frames.name: p055-text-0553
frames.text: partially (neutral gears) and the speed of the engine noted. Tacho-

frames.name: p055-text-0554
frames.text: meter should show not over 1,350 to 1,400 r. p. m.

frames.name: p055-text-0555
frames.text: Operation of each ignition head should be tested separately by

frames.name: p055-text-0556
frames.text: shutting off first one switch and then the other. The engine should

frames.name: p055-text-0557
frames.text: show the same r. p. m. in each case. With the throttle wide open,

frames.name: p055-text-0558
frames.text: whether the engine is running on one or both sets will make very

frames.name: p055-text-0559
frames.text: little difference in the speed (possible 10 or 15 r. p. m.). At lower

frames.name: p055-text-0560
frames.text: speeds (600 to 800 r. p. m.) the effect will be more apparent.

frames.name: p055-text-0561
frames.text: Before stopping the engine, throttle it down to idling speed for a

frames.name: p055-text-0562
frames.text: minute ot two, then turn the ignition switches to “off,” and at the

frames.name: p055-text-0563
frames.text: same time open the throttle wide. Opening the throttle will “choke”

frames.name: p055-text-0564
frames.text: the engine and cause it to stop immediately. Allowing the throttle

frames.name: p055-text-0565
frames.text: to remain in the idling position may permit an overheated plug or

frames.name: p055-text-0566
frames.text: particle of carbon to fire the engine spasmodically for some time after

frames.name: p055-text-0567
frames.text: the ignition is cut off.

frames.name: p055-text-0568
frames.text: Caution.—Do not attempt to crank an engine immediately after

frames.name: p055-text-0569
frames.text: it has been stopped. An overheated plug or incandescent particle

frames.name: p055-text-0570
frames.text: of carbon might cause preignition and a disastrous back kick. Allow

frames.name: p055-text-0571
frames.text: it to cool off for a few minutes.

frames.name: p055-text-0572
frames.text: COLD-WEATHER SUGGESTIONS

frames.name: p055-text-0573
frames.text: 1. Inspect the engine carefully, as instructed on pages 57 to 65.

frames.name: p055-text-0574
frames.text: 2. Put 3 gallons of hot lubricating oil into the engine crank case.

frames.name: p055-text-0575
frames.text: Oil should be heated in an open-top container set into boiling water.

frames.name: p055-text-0576
frames.text: 3. Put a sufficient quantity of hot oil into the oil reservoir, so that

frames.name: p055-text-0577
frames.text: the reservoir will be about two-thirds full after the 3 gallons placed

frames.name: p055-text-0578
frames.text: in the crank case have been pumped back into it.

frames.name: p055-text-0579
frames.text: 4. Remove the vent plug in the side of the oil-pump body so that

frames.name: p055-text-0580
frames.text: the hot oil may run in to prime the pump.

frames.name: p055-text-0581
frames.text: 5. Fill the cooling system with boiling water. Soft water should

frames.name: p055-text-0582
frames.text: be used wherever available. Do not use any antifreeze preparation.

frames.name: p055-text-0583
frames.text: 6. Prime the engine and start at slow speed with the throttle par-

frames.name: p055-text-0584
frames.text: tially closed.

frames.name: p056-text-0586
frames.text: Plate No. 39

frames.name: p056-text-0587
frames.text: CAMSHAFT ASSEMBLY

frames.name: p057-text-0589
frames.text: 7. Accelerate and slow down the engine occasionally to throw the

frames.name: p057-text-0590
frames.text: oil up into the cylinder. Run the engine until the oil has been thor-

frames.name: p057-text-0591
frames.text: oughly distributed as indicated by the action of the oil-pressure

frames.name: p057-text-0592
frames.text: gauge and a uniform temperature of the engine. This period need

frames.name: p057-text-0593
frames.text: not be continuous, and, if possible, engines should be alternately run

frames.name: p057-text-0594
frames.text: for a few minutes, stopped for five minutes, and then restarted.

frames.name: p057-text-0595
frames.text: 8. If the machine is not run at once the engine should not be

frames.name: p057-text-0596
frames.text: allowed to remain stationary for more than 10 minutes at a time, as

frames.name: p057-text-0597
frames.text: it will get cold again.

frames.name: p057-text-0598
frames.text: TO DRAIN ENGINE

frames.name: p057-text-0599
frames.text: 9. After finishing a test or run, drain all oil and water before the

frames.name: p057-text-0600
frames.text: engine has had an opportunity to cool off. Plug No. 250 and sump

frames.name: p057-text-0601
frames.text: cover No. 8129 should be removed to drain the oil from the engine.

frames.name: p057-text-0602
frames.text: A plug of the same number (No. 250) is provided in the bottom of the

frames.name: p057-text-0603
frames.text: water pump for the purpose of draining the water.

frames.name: p057-text-0604
frames.text: 10. Spark plugs should be removed from the engine and kept in a

frames.name: p057-text-0605
frames.text: warm place if the engine is to stand idle overnight or for any con-

frames.name: p057-text-0606
frames.text: siderable period.

frames.name: p057-text-0607
frames.text: ENGINE TROUBLES

frames.name: p057-text-0608
frames.text: The diagnosing of gasoline-engine troubles is largely a matter of

frames.name: p057-text-0609
frames.text: experience on account of the fact that a symptom may be due to any

frames.name: p057-text-0610
frames.text: one of a number of causes. A correct conclusion can only be arrived

frames.name: p057-text-0611
frames.text: at by a process of elimination. The different causes, as set forth in

frames.name: p057-text-0612
frames.text: the table which follows, have been arranged in the order in which

frames.name: p057-text-0613
frames.text: they most frequently occur.

frames.name: p057-text-0614
frames.text: Try one thing at a time and in the order given in the table. Once

frames.name: p057-text-0615
frames.text: the trouble is located the remedy should be obvious. It is essential

frames.name: p057-text-0616
frames.text: that any troubles be remedied immediately when they are located;

frames.name: p057-text-0617
frames.text: otherwise serious damage or the entire failure of the engine may

frames.name: p057-text-0618
frames.text: result.

frames.name: p057-text-0619
frames.text: If the engine can not be turned over under reasonable pressure:

frames.name: p057-text-0620
frames.text: 1. Examine water pump for ice.

frames.name: p057-text-0621
frames.text: 2. Examine gears for obstruction.

frames.name: p057-text-0622
frames.text: If engine fails to start, it may be due to any one of the following

frames.name: p057-text-0623
frames.text: causes:

frames.name: p057-text-0624
frames.text: 1. Lack of gasoline.

frames.name: p057-text-0625
frames.text: Examine tank.

frames.name: p057-text-0626
frames.text: Examine shut-off cock.

frames.name: p057-text-0627
frames.text: Examine trap.

frames.name: p057-text-0628
frames.text: Examine piping.

frames.name: p057-text-0629
frames.text: Examine hose connections.

frames.name: p057-text-0630
frames.text: Examine carburetor float valve.

frames.name: p057-text-0631
frames.text: 2. Primed too heavily.

frames.name: p057-text-0632
frames.text: 3. Insufficiently primed.

frames.name: p058-text-0634
frames.text: Plate No. 40.

frames.name: p058-text-0635
frames.text: LONGITUDINAL ENGINE SECTION

frames.name: p059-text-0637
frames.text: 4. Throttle too wide open.

frames.name: p059-text-0638
frames.text: 5. Throttle not opened wide enough.

frames.name: p059-text-0639
frames.text: 6. Water in carburetor.

frames.name: p059-text-0640
frames.text: 7. Battery not up to full strength.

frames.name: p059-text-0641
frames.text: 8. Loose connection at battery, switch, distributor.

frames.name: p059-text-0642
frames.text: 9. Broken wire.
