frames.name: p059-text-0643
frames.text: 10. Dirt or moisture on outside or inside of distributor.

frames.name: p059-text-0644
frames.text: 11. Wires improperly connected.

frames.name: p059-text-0645
frames.text: 12. Ignition incorrectly timed.

frames.name: p059-text-0646
frames.text: 13. Air leak in intake manifold.

frames.name: p059-text-0647
frames.text: 14. Valves improperly timed.

frames.name: p059-text-0648
frames.text: If engine stops:

frames.name: p059-text-0650
frames.text: 1. Throttle control loosened up or disconnected.

frames.name: p059-text-0651
frames.text: 2. Overheated.

frames.name: p059-text-0652
frames.text: If engine misses:

frames.name: p059-text-0653
frames.text: 1. Loss of compression.

frames.name: p059-text-0654
frames.text: Valve sticking.

frames.name: p059-text-0655
frames.text: Valve seat caked with carbon.

frames.name: p059-text-0656
frames.text: Tappet improperly adjusted.

frames.name: p059-text-0657
frames.text: Valve warped.

frames.name: p059-text-0658
frames.text: Valve spring broken.

frames.name: p059-text-0659
frames.text: Cylinder or piston scored.

frames.name: p059-text-0660
frames.text: Rings broken or sticking.

frames.name: p059-text-0661
frames.text: 2. Spark plug loose or defective.

frames.name: p059-text-0662
frames.text: 3. Rocker arm too tight.

frames.name: p059-text-0663
frames.text: 4. High-tension insulation defective.

frames.name: p059-text-0664
frames.text: 5. Moisture or dirt in distributor.

frames.name: p059-text-0665
frames.text: 6. Water or dirt in carburetor; examine jets.

frames.name: p059-text-0666
frames.text: If engine fails to develop power:

frames.name: p059-text-0667
frames.text: 1. Insufficient throttle opening.

frames.name: p059-text-0668
frames.text: 2. Insufficient spark advance.

frames.name: p059-text-0669
frames.text: 3. Insufficient gasoline supply.

frames.name: p059-text-0670
frames.text: Piping or stop-cock capacity too small.

frames.name: p059-text-0671
frames.text: Obstruction in piping.

frames.name: p059-text-0672
frames.text: Obstruction in trap.

frames.name: p059-text-0673
frames.text: Pressure leak.

frames.name: p059-text-0674
frames.text: Insufficient pressure—if pressure-feed system.

frames.name: p059-text-0675
frames.text: Obstruction in one or more jets.

frames.name: p059-text-0676
frames.text: 4. Improper carburetor adjustment. (See carburetor.)

frames.name: p059-text-0677
frames.text: 5. One or more cylinders missing fire. (See above.)

frames.name: p059-text-0678
frames.text: 6. Engine overheated. (See below.)

frames.name: p059-text-0679
frames.text: 7. Air leaks—intake manifold.

frames.name: p059-text-0680
frames.text: 8. Obstruction in carburetor intake.

frames.name: p059-text-0681
frames.text: 9. Water in gasoline.

frames.name: p060-text-0683
frames.text: Plate No. 41

frames.name: p060-text-0684
frames.text: DISTRIBUTOR END OF ENGINE

frames.name: p061-text-0002
frames.text: 10. Excessive carbon.

frames.name: p061-text-0003
frames.text: 11. Poor gasoline.

frames.name: p061-text-0004
frames.text: 12. Weak battery or defective generator.

frames.name: p061-text-0005
frames.text: 13. Exhaust manifold or pipes of insufficient capacity.

frames.name: p061-text-0006
frames.text: If engine overheats:

frames.name: p061-text-0007
frames.text: 1. Insufficient water.

frames.name: p061-text-0008
frames.text: 2. Insufficient radiator area or capacity due to covered

frames.name: p061-text-0009
frames.text: radiator.

frames.name: p061-text-0010
frames.text: 3. Water pipes dented or broken.

frames.name: p061-text-0011
frames.text: 4. Obstruction in water piping or radiator.

frames.name: p061-text-0012
frames.text: 5. Failure of water pump.

frames.name: p061-text-0013
frames.text: 6. Insufficient oil.

frames.name: p061-text-0014
frames.text: 7. Failure of oiling system.

frames.name: p061-text-0015
frames.text: 8. Improper carburetor adjustment.

frames.name: p061-text-0016
frames.text: 9. Excessive carbon.

frames.name: p061-text-0017
frames.text: ENGINE INSPECTION

frames.name: p061-text-0018
frames.text: To insure engines rendering the maximum service they must be in-

frames.name: p061-text-0019
frames.text: spected daily or at least after every five hours’ run. It is advisable

frames.name: p061-text-0020
frames.text: that these inspections be systematically carried out and that the in-

frames.name: p061-text-0021
frames.text: spector or squad foreman be provided with a form covering the

frames.name: p061-text-0022
frames.text: points set forth in the chapter following. Inspectors should be in-

frames.name: p061-text-0023
frames.text: structed to rigidly adhere to this form and check the different items

frames.name: p061-text-0024
frames.text: off as they are attended to.

frames.name: p061-text-0025
frames.text: 1. Examine all valve springs carefully.

frames.name: p061-text-0026
frames.text: 2. Squirt a little light oil through the valve springs onto each valve

frames.name: p061-text-0027
frames.text: stem.

frames.name: p061-text-0028
frames.text: 3. Examine throttle, spark and all other adjustment controls. Be

frames.name: p061-text-0029
frames.text: sure that they work freely; permit full throw of throttles and distribu-

frames.name: p061-text-0030
frames.text: tors that have not become excessively loose.

frames.name: p061-text-0031
frames.text: 4. Test all cylinders for compression.

frames.name: p061-text-0032
frames.text: 5. Try rocker arms—they should all be free when the valves which

frames.name: p061-text-0033
frames.text: they operate are seated.

frames.name: p061-text-0034
frames.text: 6. Check tappet gap of all valves-piston at firing point.

frames.name: p061-text-0035
frames.text: 7. Check valve timing with timing disk.

frames.name: p061-text-0036
frames.text: COOLING SYSTEM

frames.name: p061-text-0037
frames.text: 8. Examine radiator, water piping, pump, water jackets, and all

frames.name: p061-text-0038
frames.text: connections for leaks.

frames.name: p061-text-0039
frames.text: 9. Fill cooling system.

frames.name: p061-text-0040
frames.text: Note.—If temperature is below freezing, follow cold weather
frames.pdf_text: NOTE.—If temperature is below freezing, follow cold weather

frames.name: p061-text-0041
frames.text: instructions on page 55.

frames.name: p061-text-0042
frames.text: GASOLINE SYSTEM

frames.name: p061-text-0043
frames.text: 10. Examine tanks, trap, piping, and all connections for leaks.

frames.name: p061-text-0044
frames.text: 11. Drain water trap.

frames.name: p061-text-0045
frames.text: 12. Fill gasoline tanks.

frames.name: p062-text-0047
frames.text: Plate No. 42

frames.name: p062-text-0048
frames.text: PROPELLER END OF ENGINE (AVIATION TYPE)

frames.name: p063-text-0050
frames.text: OILING SYSTEM

frames.name: p063-text-0051
frames.text: 13. Drain system by taking out plug No. 8133.

frames.name: p063-text-0052
frames.text: 14. Remove rear pump cover plate which will release oil-pump

frames.name: p063-text-0053
frames.text: screen No. 8220.

frames.name: p063-text-0054
frames.text: 15. Clean screen thoroughly with a brush and gasoline.

frames.name: p063-text-0055
frames.text: 16. Replace screen and cover plate using a new gasket, No. 8382,

frames.name: p063-text-0056
frames.text: if the old one was damaged in removing cover.

frames.name: p063-text-0057
frames.text: 17. Examine reservoir, cooler, and all piping and connection for

frames.name: p063-text-0058
frames.text: leaks.

frames.name: p063-text-0059
frames.text: 18. Oil thrust bearing.

frames.name: p063-text-0060
frames.text: 19. Replace all hose connections, either for water, oil, or gasoline,

frames.name: p063-text-0061
frames.text: which show any signs of deterioration.

frames.name: p063-text-0062
frames.text: ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT

frames.name: p063-text-0063
frames.text: 20. Examine all electrical connections at generator, regulator,

frames.name: p063-text-0064
frames.text: switch, battery, and distributor to see that they are clean and tight.

frames.name: p063-text-0065
frames.text: 21. Examine all wiring to see that insulation has not become

frames.name: p063-text-0066
frames.text: abraded.

frames.name: p063-text-0067
frames.text: 22. Clean distributors as instructed on page 67.

frames.name: p063-text-0068
frames.text: 23. Oil generator and tachometer drive.

frames.name: p063-text-0069
frames.text: 24. Examine plugs for cracked or loose porcelains. This should

frames.name: p063-text-0070
frames.text: preferably be done immediately after the engine is stopped and while

frames.name: p063-text-0071
frames.text: the plugs are still hot.

frames.name: p063-text-0072
frames.text: 25. Check contact-breaker clearance and examine contact points.

frames.name: p063-text-0073
frames.text: 26. Check timing of ignition and synchronization of distributors.

frames.name: p063-text-0074
frames.text: Caution.—Leave the ignition switches and the gasoline shut-off

frames.name: p063-text-0075
frames.text: cock in the “off” position.

frames.name: p063-text-0076
frames.text: If the switches are left “on,” the battery will discharge through the

frames.name: p063-text-0077
frames.text: ignition system and generator, and it will be necessary to either

frames.name: p063-text-0078
frames.text: recharge or replace it before the engine can be started again. With

frames.name: p063-text-0079
frames.text: both switches turned off, the ammeter needle should stand approxi-

frames.name: p063-text-0080
frames.text: mately at zero.

frames.name: p063-text-0081
frames.text: ENGINE OVERHAUL

frames.name: p063-text-0082
frames.text: U. S. A. standardized engines are made up of a combination of

frames.name: p063-text-0083
frames.text: units or assemblies, and the units in turn of a number of subassem-

frames.name: p063-text-0084
frames.text: blies. In the chapters which follow the various units are described

frames.name: p063-text-0085
frames.text: in the order in which they should be dismounted.

frames.name: p063-text-0086
frames.text: A list of parts (names and numbers) composing each unit is in the

frames.name: p063-text-0087
frames.text: back of the book.

frames.name: p063-text-0088
frames.text: It will be found that time and space can be saved and confusion

frames.name: p063-text-0089
frames.text: of parts avoided if each assembly be disassembled, inspected, and

frames.name: p063-text-0090
frames.text: overhauled as it is dismounted. Then assembled and laid to one

frames.name: p063-text-0091
frames.text: side until such time as the whole engine is ready to reassemble.

frames.name: p063-text-0092
frames.text: The combining of the subassemblies into a complete engine is out-

frames.name: p063-text-0093
frames.text: lined on page 101.

frames.name: p064-text-0095
frames.text: Plate No. 43

frames.name: p064-text-0096
frames.text: OUTLINE DIMENSIONS (AVIATION MOUNT SHOWN)

frames.name: p065-text-0098
frames.text: Shorter and better methods of handling the work may be developed,

frames.name: p065-text-0099
frames.text: but, in the main, the plan outlined here will be found most satis-

frames.name: p065-text-0100
frames.text: factory.

frames.name: p065-text-0101
frames.text: A bench or other suitable place on which parts and tools may be

frames.name: p065-text-0102
frames.text: laid out should be provided.

frames.name: p065-text-0103
frames.text: The mechanic should form the habit of laying out his tools in a

frames.name: p065-text-0104
frames.text: definite order so that the one desired may be readily reached.

frames.name: p065-text-0105
frames.text: Have a bucket of kerosene handy in which parts may be washed.

frames.name: p065-text-0106
frames.text: Waste should not be used for wiping parts. Threads or lint are

frames.name: p065-text-0107
frames.text: likely to stick to the surfaces and eventually find their way into oil

frames.name: p065-text-0108
frames.text: passages. Pieces of clean cloth or rags are preferable.

frames.name: p065-text-0109
frames.text: Nuts such as those used to hold the cylinders down on the crank

frames.name: p065-text-0110
frames.text: case should be screwed onto their proper studs after disassembling—

frames.name: p065-text-0111
frames.text: not only to protect the studs but to avoid confusion in reassembling.

frames.name: p065-text-0112
frames.text: Cotter pins and lock wires which have been badly bent should not

frames.name: p065-text-0113
frames.text: be used again.

frames.name: p065-text-0114
frames.text: Great care should be taken to prevent pieces of cotter pins, lock

frames.name: p065-text-0115
frames.text: wire, chips, or any small parts from falling into the crank case or any

frames.name: p065-text-0116
frames.text: part of the engine. They might work into the gears or oil passages

frames.name: p065-text-0117
frames.text: and cause immeasurable damage.

frames.name: p065-text-0118
frames.text: Have an oil can, full of clean oil, handy at all times. Oil all

frames.name: p065-text-0119
frames.text: bearing surfaces before assembling.

frames.name: p065-text-0120
frames.text: Oil all parts which are press or drive fit.

frames.name: p065-text-0121
frames.text: Oil all bolt and stud threads.

frames.name: p065-text-0122
frames.text: Exhaust manifold studs should be greased with a graphite paste.

frames.name: p065-text-0123
frames.text: Each step in the process of assembling should be finished as the

frames.name: p065-text-0124
frames.text: work progresses. Do not leave a bolt loose or a nut not cottered

frames.name: p065-text-0125
frames.text: with the idea of coming back to it later on.

frames.name: p065-text-0126
frames.text: Never “slack off” or loosen a nut in order to line up the notch in

frames.name: p065-text-0127
frames.text: the nut with the cotter pin hole in the bolt or stud. If it cannot be

frames.name: p065-text-0128
frames.text: tightened still further with reasonable effort in order to bring the

frames.name: p065-text-0129
frames.text: next notch in line, replace it with another nut.

frames.name: p065-text-0130
frames.text: All subassemblies, as they are overhauled and put together, should

frames.name: p065-text-0131
frames.text: be covered to protect them from dust and dirt.

frames.name: p065-text-0132
frames.text: DISTRIBUTORS

frames.name: p065-text-0133
frames.text: To return to the distributors—the circuit-breaker mechanism for

frames.name: p065-text-0134
frames.text: each head is identical with that used in any high-grade magneto

frames.name: p065-text-0135
frames.text: with two exceptions, as follows:

frames.name: p065-text-0136
frames.text: Two main circuit breakers, connected in parallel, are provided

frames.name: p065-text-0137
frames.text: instead of one. The two breakers are timed to operate simultane-

frames.name: p065-text-0138
frames.text: ously and are provided in duplicate as a precautionary measure.

frames.name: p065-text-0139
frames.text: An auxiliary circuit breaker, the function of which is to prevent the

frames.name: p065-text-0140
frames.text: production of a spark when the engine is turned backward or “rocked,”

frames.name: p066-text-0143
frames.text: Plate No. 44

frames.name: p066-text-0144
frames.text: CRANK-CASE DIMENSIONS (AVIATION MOUNT SHOWN)

frames.name: p067-text-0146
frames.text: is also provided. This auxiliary breaker is connected in parallel

frames.name: p067-text-0147
frames.text: with the other two through a resistance unit which reduces the amount

frames.name: p067-text-0148
frames.text: of current flowing through it. The breaker is so timed that it opens

frames.name: p067-text-0149
frames.text: slightly before the other two when the engine is turned in a forward

frames.name: p067-text-0150
frames.text: direction. The opening of the main breakers then results in the pro-

frames.name: p067-text-0151
frames.text: duction of a spark. When the engine is turned in a backward direc-

frames.name: p067-text-0152
frames.text: tion the two main breakers open first and no spark is produced, due

frames.name: p067-text-0153
frames.text: to the fact that the current continues to flow through the coil through

frames.name: p067-text-0154
frames.text: the auxiliary breaker but in diminished quantity, due to the resistance

frames.name: p067-text-0155
frames.text: unit. By the time the circuit is opened at the auxiliary breaker, the

frames.name: p067-text-0156
frames.text: intensity of the magnetic field of the coil has weakened to such an

frames.name: p067-text-0157
frames.text: extent that no spark is produced. A transformer coil is inccrporated

frames.name: p067-text-0158
frames.text: in the Bakelite cover of each distributor head.

frames.name: p067-text-0159
frames.text: HIGH-TENSION WIRING—DISASSEMBLING AND INSPECTION

frames.name: p067-text-0160
frames.text: Disconnect all high-tension cables from the spark plugs.

frames.name: p067-text-0161
frames.text: Remove the screws No. 201 which hold the cable tube clips No.

frames.name: p067-text-0162
frames.text: 12283 in place.

frames.name: p067-text-0163
frames.text: Release four clips and unscrew two composition nuts on each dis-

frames.name: p067-text-0164
frames.text: tributor head.

frames.name: p067-text-0165
frames.text: The distributor head, cables, and cable tube may now be lifted

frames.name: p067-text-0166
frames.text: off together. They should be handled carefully to prevent any possi-

frames.name: p067-text-0167
frames.text: bility of breaking the distributor covers and damage to the cable.

frames.name: p067-text-0168
frames.text: Examine these cables carefully, especially at any point where they

frames.name: p067-text-0169
frames.text: may be sent sharply or where they may come in contact with any

frames.name: p067-text-0170
frames.text: metal parts. See that the insulation is intact and that the terminals

frames.name: p067-text-0171
frames.text: are firmly attached.

frames.name: p067-text-0172
frames.text: Examine inside surface of distributor cover and particularly the

frames.name: p067-text-0173
frames.text: contact segments and the path of the rotor brush. The surface

frames.name: p067-text-0174
frames.text: should be smooth and free from scores or scratches.

frames.name: p067-text-0175
frames.text: Wipe out any carbon dust carefully with a soft cloth moistened

frames.name: p067-text-0176
frames.text: with alcohol or gasoline.

frames.name: p067-text-0177
frames.text: Examine the distributor shaft for lost motion between the dis-

frames.name: p067-text-0178
frames.text: tributor driving flange and the driver. This should not be more than

frames.name: p067-text-0179
frames.text: enough to allow about one-sixteenth-inch motion at the end of the

frames.name: p067-text-0180
frames.text: rotor arm.

frames.name: p067-text-0181
frames.text: DISTRIBUTOR BASE

frames.name: p067-text-0182
frames.text: Disconnect the cross reach No. 8333 between the two distributor

frames.name: p067-text-0183
frames.text: assemblies and take out bolts No. 116 from the distributor-base

frames.name: p067-text-0184
frames.text: flanges. This will permit the distributor-base assemblies to be

frames.name: p067-text-0185
frames.text: taken off.

frames.name: p067-text-0186
frames.text: Check the gap on each breaker with a thickness gauge. This can

frames.name: p067-text-0187
frames.text: best be done with the breaker block on the wide lobe of the cam.

frames.name: p067-text-0188
frames.text: The gap for all three breakers should be from 0.010 to 0.013.

frames.name: p068-text-0190
frames.text: Examine the condition of the contact points. These points should

frames.name: p068-text-0191
frames.text: be bright, and in case they have become pitted to any extent they

frames.name: p068-text-0192
frames.text: can be smoothed down on an oilstone. They are very hard and it

frames.name: p068-text-0193
frames.text: will be impossible to file them.

frames.name: p068-text-0194
frames.text: Examine the rubber buffers against which the breaker-arm springs

frames.name: p068-text-0195
frames.text: bear. These rubber buffers are vulcanized to the breaker arm, and

frames.name: p068-text-0196
frames.text: in case they have deteriorated to any extent due to contact with oil

frames.name: p068-text-0197
frames.text: the whole breaker-arm assembly should be replaced.

frames.name: p068-text-0198
frames.text: Examine the breaker-arm springs. Be sure that they have not

frames.name: p068-text-0199
frames.text: begun to crack around the slotted hole through which they are bolted

frames.name: p068-text-0200
frames.text: to the bus bar. The tension of the spring on the auxiliary or middle

frames.name: p068-text-0201
frames.text: Plate No. 45

frames.name: p068-text-0202
frames.text: DIMENSIONS FRONT ELEVATION (AVIATION MOUNTING)

frames.name: p069-text-0204
frames.text: breaker should be from 16 to 20 ounces when the contact is open.

frames.name: p069-text-0205
frames.text: The tension on the main breaker-arm springs should be from 28 to

frames.name: p069-text-0206
frames.text: 30 ounces when the contact is open.

frames.name: p069-text-0207
frames.text: Examine the resistance unit through which the current passes to

frames.name: p069-text-0208
frames.text: the middle breaker. The coils of this resistance unit should be

frames.name: p069-text-0209
frames.text: separated throughout the length of the unit. If the coils of resist-

frames.name: p069-text-0210
frames.text: ance wire come in contact with one another, the total resistance of

frames.name: p069-text-0211
frames.text: the unit will be decreased and the proper functioning of the middle

frames.name: p069-text-0212
frames.text: breaker will be impaired.

frames.name: p069-text-0213
frames.text: Examine the condition of the face of the cam. This should not

frames.name: p069-text-0214
frames.text: show excessive wear and should be nicely burnished.

frames.name: p069-text-0215
frames.text: Examine the condition of the fiber blocks which bear against the

frames.name: p069-text-0216
frames.text: cam surface. The fiber should extend approximately

frames.name: p069-text-0220
frames.text: -inch beyond

frames.name: p069-text-0221
frames.text: the metal and show a smooth bearing surface.

frames.name: p069-text-0222
frames.text: Examine the carbon brush in the end of the rotor arm. If the

frames.name: p069-text-0223
frames.text: brush has worn down to such an extent that it is less than ¼-inch

frames.name: p069-text-0224
frames.text: long, a new brush should be fitted. In putting in the new brush

frames.name: p069-text-0225
frames.text: and spring, press the brush into place in the rotor arm with a small

frames.name: p069-text-0226
frames.text: punch as far as possible. This will properly seat the spring and will

frames.name: p069-text-0227
frames.text: prevent the brush from extending too far out of the guide. The

frames.name: p069-text-0228
frames.text: rotor brush is a special composition and requires no lubrication.

frames.name: p069-text-0229
frames.text: Examine the ball bearings which carry the distributor cam shaft

frames.name: p069-text-0230
frames.text: for radial and lateral lost motion. This should be only barely per-

frames.name: p069-text-0231
frames.text: ceptible. If it is deemed advisable to replace one or both of these

frames.name: p069-text-0232
frames.text: bearings, the rotor arm should be removed by taking out the screw D

frames.name: p069-text-0233
frames.text: (see fig. 16). The shaft may now be driven out through the cam.

frames.name: p069-text-0234
frames.text: This should be done with a small punch which will permit the key to

frames.name: p069-text-0235
frames.text: remain in the cam. In reassembling the distributor the bearings

frames.name: p069-text-0236
frames.text: should be packed with vaseline and the felt washer with which each

frames.name: p069-text-0237
frames.text: cam is filled should be thoroughly saturated with a good light oil.

frames.name: p069-text-0238
frames.text: This oil will work out through the small holes drilled in the face of

frames.name: p069-text-0239
frames.text: the cam and will properly lubricate the contact arm blocks. It is

frames.name: p069-text-0240
frames.text: advisable also to put a little vaseline or thin grease on the outside

frames.name: p069-text-0241
frames.text: surface of the cam. The studs on which the contact arms are mounted

frames.name: p069-text-0242
frames.text: should also be oiled. Be sure that the contact points are properly

frames.name: p069-text-0243
frames.text: adjusted and the lock nuts are drawn up snugly.

frames.name: p069-text-0244
frames.text: The transformer coil is built into the distributor housing cover.

frames.name: p069-text-0245
frames.text: All connections are made inside and the whole is covered by a fiber

frames.name: p069-text-0246
frames.text: plate which is sealed in place. It is not advisable to remove this

frames.name: p069-text-0247
frames.text: cover plate for any purpose whatsoever.

frames.name: p069-text-0248
frames.text: In replacing the rotor arm be sure that the drive pin in the cam

frames.name: p069-text-0249
frames.text: properly enters the hole in the arm.

frames.name: p069-text-0250
frames.text: Information as to timing and adjusting the distributor assemblies

frames.name: p069-text-0251
frames.text: will be found under the heading of “Timing ignition” (p. 107).

frames.name: p070-text-0253
frames.text: TO DISMOUNT THE GENERATOR

frames.name: p070-text-0254
frames.text: Remove the four nuts No. 101 and washers No. 111, which will

frames.name: p070-text-0255
frames.text: permit the generator to be lifted off.

frames.name: p070-text-0256
frames.text: DISASSEMBLING AND INSPECTION

frames.name: p070-text-0257
frames.text: Examine the condition of the splines or keys on the lower end of

frames.name: p070-text-0258
frames.text: the shaft. These should not show undue wear.

frames.name: p070-text-0259
frames.text: The tachometer drive assembly complete can be removed by

frames.name: p070-text-0260
frames.text: screwing out the bearing assembly (see engine illustration). This

frames.name: p070-text-0261
frames.text: will permit the worm-gear shaft to be withdrawn. The worm gear

frames.name: p070-text-0262
frames.text: and the bronze bushings in which the shaft runs should now be

frames.name: p070-text-0263
frames.text: examined as to their condition. They should be free from bad cuts

frames.name: p070-text-0264
frames.text: or scores. Before inserting the shaft again in the bearing the recess

frames.name: p070-text-0265
frames.text: between the two bushings should be filled with vaseline or other light

frames.name: p070-text-0266
frames.text: grease.

frames.name: p070-text-0267
frames.text: Remove the cap from the upper end of the generator by taking off

frames.name: p070-text-0268
frames.text: the two terminal nuts.

frames.name: p070-text-0269
frames.text: Examine the condition of the commutator and brushes. In case

frames.name: p070-text-0270
frames.text: the commutator is burned or rough it should be polished with a very

frames.name: p070-text-0271
frames.text: fine piece of sandpaper. The best possible condition of the commu-

frames.name: p070-text-0272
frames.text: tator is shown when it takes the form of a bluish polish, which should

frames.name: p070-text-0273
frames.text: not be mistaken for a burned commutator. When the commutator

frames.name: p070-text-0274
frames.text: carries a blue polish on it, it should be allowed to remain this way and

frames.name: p070-text-0275
frames.text: only receive an occasional wiping off with a soft rag.

frames.name: p070-text-0276
frames.text: In case the commutator is badly cut or scored, it should be turned

frames.name: p070-text-0277
frames.text: down in a lathe a sufficient amount to smooth it up. The mica should

frames.name: p070-text-0278
frames.text: then be “undercut.” This work should only be done at a base repair

frames.name: p070-text-0279
frames.text: shop and by experienced mechanics. If the commutator was found

frames.name: p070-text-0280
frames.text: to be scored, the brushes will also be in bad condition. These brushes

frames.name: p070-text-0281
frames.text: are soldered to the brush holders and in case of a replacement a new

frames.name: p070-text-0282
frames.text: brush holder and brush should be fitted. Brushes that have been

frames.name: p070-text-0283
frames.text: roughed up or new brushed should be sanded to fit on the commutator

frames.name: p070-text-0284
frames.text: by wrapping a strip of very fine sandpaper at least halfway around the

frames.name: p070-text-0285
frames.text: commutator and drawing it through one brush at a time. This will

frames.name: p070-text-0286
frames.text: form the brush to the curvature of the commutator. It is essential

frames.name: p070-text-0287
frames.text: that the brushes properly fit the commutator and the work should

frames.name: p070-text-0288
frames.text: only be done by an experienced mechanic.

frames.name: p070-text-0289
frames.text: Examine the wire leading from the field coils to the generator

frames.name: p070-text-0290
frames.text: terminal and its connection with this terminal. Any dirt or excess

frames.name: p070-text-0291
frames.text: oil should be wiped off before replacing the cap.

frames.name: p070-text-0292
frames.text: The ball bearing on the upper end of the generator shaft can be

frames.name: p070-text-0293
frames.text: lubricated through the oil cup in the cap.

frames.name: p070-text-0294
frames.text: This bearing should receive a few drops of oil after every long run,

frames.name: p070-text-0295
frames.text: but should not be lubricated excessively, as the oil is likely to run

frames.name: p070-text-0296
frames.text: down over the commutator.

frames.name: p071-text-0298
frames.text: VOLTAGE REGULATOR

frames.name: p071-text-0299
frames.text: This device, which is typical design, consists of an iron core on which

frames.name: p071-text-0300
frames.text: are wound three coils, the connections of which are shown on the

frames.name: p071-text-0301
frames.text: circuit diagram. The frame of the regulator carries a pivoted arma-

frames.name: p071-text-0302
frames.text: ture fitted with adjustable contact points at one end. The con-

frames.name: p071-text-0303
frames.text: tact points are normally held together by an adjustable spring.

frames.name: p071-text-0304
frames.text: The function of the voltage regulator is to prevent the generator

frames.name: p071-text-0305
frames.text: from delivering more than a predetermined supply of electricity.

frames.name: p071-text-0306
frames.text: The regulator will need practically no attention with the exception

frames.name: p071-text-0307
frames.text: of an occasional checking up of the constant separation and the

frames.name: p071-text-0308
frames.text: length of the brass pin set into the opposite end of the armature.

frames.name: p071-text-0309
frames.text: This pin should extend from 0.043 to 0.045 inch above the surface of

frames.name: p071-text-0310
frames.text: the armature. When the armature is pressed down so that this pin

frames.name: p071-text-0311
frames.text: bears against the end of the core, the gap between the contact points

frames.name: p071-text-0312
frames.text: should be from 0.005 to 0.007 inch. If the contacts are burned or

frames.name: p071-text-0313
frames.text: pitted they may be smoothed down with an oilstone. The tension

frames.name: p071-text-0314
frames.text: of the adjusting spring should not be altered except by an expert and

frames.name: p071-text-0315
frames.text: with the aid of proper instruments. See that all terminals are clean

frames.name: p071-text-0316
frames.text: and tight.

frames.name: p071-text-0317
frames.text: IGNITION SWITCH

frames.name: p071-text-0318
frames.text: The ignition switch should be inspected each time the engine is

frames.name: p071-text-0319
frames.text: taken down for overhauling.

frames.name: p071-text-0320
frames.text: Two resistance units are mounted on the back of the ignition

frames.name: p071-text-0321
frames.text: switch. These units should be examined to see that the coils do not

frames.name: p071-text-0322
frames.text: Plate No. 46

frames.name: p071-text-0323
frames.text: IGNITION SWITCH

frames.name: p072-text-0325
frames.text: come in contact with one another. If this should happen the total

frames.name: p072-text-0326
frames.text: resistance of each unit would be reduced, which would result in the

frames.name: p072-text-0327
frames.text: burning of the distributor contact points. It would also affect the

frames.name: p072-text-0328
frames.text: proper functioning of the auxiliary contact arm in the distributor.

frames.name: p072-text-0329
frames.text: If these resistance units should burn out entirely it would shut off

frames.name: p072-text-0330
frames.text: the ignition.

frames.name: p072-text-0331
frames.text: The three screws A should be removed and the switch contacts

frames.name: p072-text-0332
frames.text: under the cover examined to see that they have the proper tension

frames.name: p072-text-0333
frames.text: and that they are clean.

frames.name: p072-text-0334
frames.text: The ammeter which is part of the switch should require no atten-

frames.name: p072-text-0335
frames.text: tion. In case the pointer sticks the instrument should be replaced,

frames.name: p072-text-0336
frames.text: as it is very important that the ammeter should indicate accurately,

frames.name: p072-text-0337
frames.text: so that the exact condition of the generator, voltage regulator, and

frames.name: p072-text-0338
frames.text: the ignition can be determined.

frames.name: p072-text-0339
frames.text: It is advisable that the replacing of a resistance unit or an ammeter

frames.name: p072-text-0340
frames.text: be done at the base repair shop.

frames.name: p072-text-0341
frames.text: Caution.—Always leave the ignition switches in the “off” position.

frames.name: p072-text-0342
frames.text: CARBURETOR

frames.name: p072-text-0343
frames.text: Two ball and ball double vertical carburetors are used on each

frames.name: p072-text-0344
frames.text: Mark VIII machine. These operate as follows:

frames.name: p072-text-0345
frames.text: The carburetor has two important functions to perform:

frames.name: p072-text-0346
frames.text: First. To deliver to all the cylinders of the engine at all times a

frames.name: p072-text-0347
frames.text: mixture of gasoline and air of the right quality to meet the require-

frames.name: p072-text-0348
frames.text: ments in the matter of power and economy.

frames.name: p072-text-0349
frames.text: Second. To so thoroughly atomize the gasoline and mix it with air

frames.name: p072-text-0350
frames.text: in the carburetor that when it reaches the intake header there will be

frames.name: p072-text-0351
frames.text: equal amounts of gasoline going to all the cylinders.

frames.name: p072-text-0352
frames.text: Note.—The first function is largely dependent on the efficiency of
frames.pdf_text: NOTE.—The first function is largely dependent on the efficiency of

frames.name: p072-text-0353
frames.text: the second and can not be satisfactory unless the second is properly

frames.name: p072-text-0354
frames.text: arranged.

frames.name: p072-text-0355
frames.text: The unusual conditions under which the Mark VIII tractor oper-

frames.name: p072-text-0356
frames.text: ates (going into and climbing out of the holes on grades as steep as

frames.name: p072-text-0357
frames.text: 50°—degrees not per cent) make it necessary that the carburetor

frames.name: p072-text-0358
frames.text: perform another function, i. e., meet satisfactorily functions 1 and 2

frames.name: p072-text-0359
frames.text: when operating on grades of 50° uphill and down.

frames.name: p072-text-0360
frames.text: CARBURETOR DESCRIPTION

frames.name: p072-text-0361
frames.text: On page 73 is a diagrammatic section intended to illustrate the

frames.name: p072-text-0362
frames.text: principle of operation.

frames.name: p072-text-0363
frames.text: The gasoline level is indicated by the line L—L and by means of

frames.name: p072-text-0364
frames.text: a pivoted spherical float the level of gasoline remains at the center

frames.name: p072-text-0365
frames.text: of the sphere regardless of the angle of the carburetor.

frames.name: p072-text-0366
frames.text: The throat A has tubes B extending well above the gasoline level

frames.name: p072-text-0367
frames.text: inside the throat and below it on the outside in the annulus C. This

frames.name: p073-text-0369
frames.text: annulus C is connected by passage D with an intermediate mixing

frames.name: p073-text-0370
frames.text: chamber E. The chamber E has in it a vertical hollow screw G

frames.name: p073-text-0371
frames.text: closed at the top and having the gasoline orifice F and the overflow

frames.name: p073-text-0372
frames.text: orifices H located at or a trifle below the gasoline level. The air

frames.name: p073-text-0373
frames.text: passage M connects the chamber E with the space below the throat

frames.name: p073-text-0374
frames.text: through the orifice N. The by-pass orifice P connects through O

frames.name: p073-text-0375
frames.text: with the passage D, and this orifice P is located just above an orifice

frames.name: p073-text-0376
frames.text: R in the throttle Q. An air valve S is shown, but this is not an

frames.name: p073-text-0377
frames.text: essential element. Its use and purpose will be explained later.

frames.name: p073-text-0378
frames.text: The suction impulses of the engine produce a partial vacuum in

frames.name: p073-text-0379
frames.text: the intake header which is communicated to the carburetor and

frames.name: p073-text-0380
frames.text: induces a flow of air through the throat A and the tubes B. The

frames.name: p073-text-0381
frames.text: flow of air through A owing to its ejector effect on the tubes B in-

frames.name: p073-text-0382
frames.text: duces a much higher vacuum in B than in the space above the throat

frames.name: p073-text-0383
frames.text: A. This added force is of great importance in breaking up the gaso-

frames.name: p073-text-0384
frames.text: line. The vacuum in the tubes B is communicated through the

frames.name: p073-text-0385
frames.text: Plate No. 47

frames.name: p073-text-0386
frames.text: SECTION THROUGH CARBURETOR

frames.name: p074-text-0389
frames.text: annulus C and the passage D to the intermediate mixing chamber E,

frames.name: p074-text-0390
frames.text: in which the vacuum is somewhat lower than in the tubes B because

frames.name: p074-text-0391
frames.text: of the flow of air through the orifice N and the passage M to E.

frames.name: p074-text-0392
frames.text: The vacuum in E extends through the overflow orifices H to the gaso-

frames.name: p074-text-0393
frames.text: line orifice F and causes gasoline to flow from the float chamber

frames.name: p074-text-0394
frames.text: through the hole J and the metering orifice F and the holes H to the

frames.name: p074-text-0395
frames.text: chamber E where it is mixed with air from M and in the form of foam

frames.name: p074-text-0396
frames.text: is drawn through D and out of the tubes B in such a broken-up con-

frames.name: p074-text-0397
frames.text: dition that complete atomization is easily effected by the main air

frames.name: p074-text-0398
frames.text: stream through throat A.

frames.name: p074-text-0399
frames.text: The reason why this carburetor requires no compensating device is

frames.name: p074-text-0400
frames.text: that the overflow point is at or a trifle below the gasoline level, and

frames.name: p074-text-0401
frames.text: as there is no initial head (or elevation of the overflow point above

frames.name: p074-text-0402
frames.text: the gasoline level) to overcome gasoline begins to flow simultaneously

frames.name: p074-text-0403
frames.text: with the air flow, and as the law governing the flow of gasoline

frames.name: p074-text-0404
frames.text: through the orifice F and air through the throat A are identical it

frames.name: p074-text-0405
frames.text: follows that the quality will be uniform throughout the full range of

frames.name: p074-text-0406
frames.text: operation.

frames.name: p074-text-0407
frames.text: Plate No. 48

frames.name: p074-text-0408
frames.text: CARBURETOR JETS AND VALVES

frames.name: p075-text-0410
frames.text: At idling speeds the velocity of air through the throat A is not great

frames.name: p075-text-0411
frames.text: enough to be positive in its action in carrying the gasoline up to the

frames.name: p075-text-0412
frames.text: throttle valve Q. To take care of this condition a by-pass P is

frames.name: p075-text-0413
frames.text: arranged to discharge just above an opening R in the throttle Q.

frames.name: p075-text-0414
frames.text: This by-pass with a very high vacuum at the discharge P draws a rich

frames.name: p075-text-0415
frames.text: mixture of gasoline and air through O and D from the intermediate

frames.name: p075-text-0416
frames.text: mixing chamber E. This is discharged at an angle across the orifice

frames.name: p075-text-0417
frames.text: R in throttle Q, which further breaks it up and at the same time

frames.name: p075-text-0418
frames.text: provides the correct amount of air to make the best firing mixture.

frames.name: p075-text-0419
frames.text: As the throttle is progressively opened the vacuum at P is reduced

frames.name: p075-text-0420
frames.text: and at B is increased until a point is reached where both P and B

frames.name: p075-text-0421
frames.text: are discharging. Further opening of the throttle makes all of the

frames.name: p075-text-0422
frames.text: gasoline discharge from B, but as the source of the mixture is at

frames.name: p075-text-0423
frames.text: all times the intermediate mixing chamber E there is no change of

frames.name: p075-text-0424
frames.text: law governing the flow of air or gasoline and the mixture is correct

frames.name: p075-text-0425
frames.text: at all times.

frames.name: p075-text-0426
frames.text: AIR VALVE

frames.name: p075-text-0427
frames.text: In all carburetors, and particularly in large ones, one difficulty

frames.name: p075-text-0428
frames.text: encountered is the lack of pick-up from slow speed, and “popping

frames.name: p075-text-0429
frames.text: back” through the carburetor when accelerating. This condition can

frames.name: p075-text-0430
frames.text: Plate No. 49

frames.name: p075-text-0431
frames.text: OUTLINE OF CARBURETOR

frames.name: p076-text-0433
frames.text: be improved in two ways: First, reducing the throat diameter to get

frames.name: p076-text-0434
frames.text: greater velocity of air, or second, increasing the richness of the mix-

frames.name: p076-text-0435
frames.text: ture of gasoline and air. The first reduces the power of the motor

frames.name: p076-text-0436
frames.text: except at slow speeds, and the second impairs the economy at all

frames.name: p076-text-0437
frames.text: speeds. The air valve S avoids both these difficulties. This air

frames.name: p076-text-0438
frames.text: valve is small, having a capacity small in comparison to the throat A.

frames.name: p076-text-0439
frames.text: All of the air going through the air valve is added to the amount

frames.name: p076-text-0440
frames.text: passing through the throat A so the inside diameter of the throat A

frames.name: p076-text-0441
frames.text: can be reduced considerably thereby increasing the air velocities at

frames.name: p076-text-0442
frames.text: slow speeds when the air valve is not in action. It is also evident

frames.name: p076-text-0443
frames.text: that with the air valve and the throat in action at all intermediate

frames.name: p076-text-0444
frames.text: and high speeds the quality of the mixture may be such as to give

frames.name: p076-text-0445
frames.text: maximum power and efficiency, and at slow speeds where more

frames.name: p076-text-0446
frames.text: torque is required as the air valve is closed by the spring, the mixture

frames.name: p076-text-0447
frames.text: must be slightly richer, and the ratio of these can be made to suit

frames.name: p076-text-0448
frames.text: the particular conditions encountered.

frames.name: p076-text-0449
frames.text: UNUSUAL CARBURETOR FUNCTION

frames.name: p076-text-0450
frames.text: It must be apparent that any carburetor with a float mechanism

frames.name: p076-text-0451
frames.text: back or forward of the air throat and with the discharge nozzle in

frames.name: p076-text-0452
frames.text: the throat if the top of the discharge nozzle is the overflow point that

frames.name: p076-text-0453
frames.text: carburetor can not function properly except on very small grades.

frames.name: p076-text-0454
frames.text: Attention is called to the fact that in the Mark VIII carburetor the

frames.name: p076-text-0455
frames.text: float chamber is back or forward of the air throat A but the discharge

frames.name: p076-text-0456
frames.text: nozzles B are not the overflow points. The overflow point is at H,

frames.name: p076-text-0457
frames.text: which is at the axis about which the gasoline level changes and is,

frames.name: p076-text-0458
frames.text: therefore, not affected by the changing angles.

frames.name: p076-text-0459
frames.text: Under no condition is pure liquid gasoline passing through D and

frames.name: p076-text-0460
frames.text: the tubes B but a foamy mixture of gasoline and air, so that owing

frames.name: p076-text-0461
frames.text: to its being so largely air it flows equally well through D and the

frames.name: p076-text-0462
frames.text: tubes B whether the machine is climbing a steep grade or going down

frames.name: p076-text-0463
frames.text: a steep decline.

frames.name: p076-text-0464
frames.text: The butterfly throttle valves in each carburetor are parallel and

frames.name: p076-text-0465
frames.text: interconnected by gear sectors pinned to the throttle stems. The

frames.name: p076-text-0466
frames.text: forward and rear carburetors have their throttles operated simultan-

frames.name: p076-text-0467
frames.text: eously by means of a shaft provided with an adjustment at each end

frames.name: p076-text-0468
frames.text: by means of which the pairs may be synchronized.

frames.name: p076-text-0469
frames.text: CARBURETOR ADJUSTMENTS

frames.name: p076-text-0470
frames.text: The sizes of the throats, gasoline regulating orifices, etc., having

frames.name: p076-text-0471
frames.text: been determined by the engine builder, should not be changed except

frames.name: p076-text-0472
frames.text: under extreme conditions. The numbers stamped on these parts

frames.name: p076-text-0473
frames.text: indicate their sizes.

frames.name: p077-text-0475
frames.text: The throats are marked in inches and fractions thereof. The gaso-

frames.name: p077-text-0476
frames.text: line orifices are numbered according to diameter of orifice in hun-

frames.name: p077-text-0477
frames.text: dredths of a millimeter; for instance, 180 indicates a diameter of 1.80

frames.name: p077-text-0478
frames.text: millimeters.

frames.name: p077-text-0479
frames.text: The throat and regulating screw sizes as well as air-valve setting

frames.name: p077-text-0480
frames.text: are marked on tag attached to carburetor and on carton in which

frames.name: p077-text-0481
frames.text: carburetor is shipped.

frames.name: p077-text-0482
frames.text: INSPECTION AND CARE

frames.name: p077-text-0483
frames.text: Owing to the fact that there are no small orifices in this carburetor

frames.name: p077-text-0484
frames.text: there is very little chance of its becoming clogged, but an excess of

frames.name: p077-text-0485
frames.text: water might obstruct the flow of gasoline.

frames.name: p077-text-0486
frames.text: The throttles should be examined to see that they operate properly

frames.name: p077-text-0487
frames.text: and both close at the same time. Float and mechanism must be

frames.name: p077-text-0488
frames.text: in good condition or level will fluctuate and cause unsteady per-

frames.name: p077-text-0489
frames.text: formance. A leaky float causes the gasoline to rise too high in the

frames.name: p077-text-0490
frames.text: chamber. Replace with another rather than try to repair it.

frames.name: p077-text-0491
frames.text: Extreme care must be exercised in assembling to see that all joints

frames.name: p077-text-0492
frames.text: are tight and all bolts and screws must be secured with lock washers,

frames.name: p077-text-0493
frames.text: cotter pins, or lock wires.

frames.name: p077-text-0494
frames.text: TO REMOVE WATER-OUTLET HEADERS

frames.name: p077-text-0495
frames.text: Remove the nuts, No. 101, which hold the water-outlet headers,

frames.name: p077-text-0496
frames.text: No. 12427–8, in place, and lift these headers with the extension tube

frames.name: p077-text-0497
frames.text: No. 12363 and the two hose connections off.

frames.name: p077-text-0498
frames.text: The clamps on these hose connections should be taken off and the

frames.name: p077-text-0499
frames.text: hose examined.

frames.name: p077-text-0500
frames.text: If the hose connections show any signs of deterioration they should

frames.name: p077-text-0501
frames.text: be replaced before reassembling.

frames.name: p077-text-0502
frames.text: Lay the outlet-header gaskets, No. 8153, to one side where they

frames.name: p077-text-0503
frames.text: will not be damaged.

frames.name: p077-text-0504
frames.text: TO REMOVE INTAKE HEADERS

frames.name: p077-text-0505
frames.text: Disconnect the water-inlet elbows, No. 8173, by removing the cap

frames.name: p077-text-0506
frames.text: screws, No. 201.

frames.name: p077-text-0507
frames.text: Remove the intake header nuts, No. 103, and the washers, No. 113.

frames.name: p077-text-0508
frames.text: This will permit the intake headers to be dismounted.

frames.name: p077-text-0509
frames.text: Examine the gaskets, No. 8172, and see that they do not overlap

frames.name: p077-text-0510
frames.text: the openings in the elbows, No. 8173, or the holes in the intake header.

frames.name: p077-text-0511
frames.text: If the gaskets appear to be in good condition put them back on the

frames.name: p077-text-0512
frames.text: studs in their former position and screw on the nuts to hold them in

frames.name: p077-text-0513
frames.text: place.

frames.name: p077-text-0514
frames.text: Leave the water-connection elbows and hose connections attached

frames.name: p077-text-0515
frames.text: to the cylinders.

frames.name: p078-text-0517
frames.text: CAM-SHAFT HOUSING UNITS

frames.name: p078-text-0518
frames.text: Each of the two assemblies consists of a cam shaft with its bearings

frames.name: p078-text-0519
frames.text: and gear—the rocker levers—a cam-shaft housing with its covers and

frames.name: p078-text-0520
frames.text: the cam-shaft drive shaft with its gear, bearings, and housing. The

frames.name: p078-text-0521
frames.text: assembly also includes all bolts, nuts, cotter pins, and small parts

frames.name: p078-text-0522
frames.text: enumerated in the parts list at the end of this chapter.

frames.name: p078-text-0523
frames.text: All parts of the two assemblies (right and left) are identical and

frames.name: p078-text-0524
frames.text: interchangeable with the exception of the cam shafts themselves and

frames.name: p078-text-0525
frames.text: the cam-shaft housing covers.

frames.name: p078-text-0526
frames.text: Each shaft is stamped with a serial number on the plug in the end

frames.name: p078-text-0527
frames.text: opposite the flanged end. Right-hand shafts bear the letter R and

frames.name: p078-text-0528
frames.text: left-hand shafts bear the letter L.

frames.name: p078-text-0529
frames.text: Plate No. 50

frames.name: p078-text-0530
frames.text: VALVE ROCKER ARM

frames.name: p079-text-0532
frames.text: The housing covers are machined in place on the housing and con-

frames.name: p079-text-0533
frames.text: sequently will not interchange.

frames.name: p079-text-0534
frames.text: DISASSEMBLING AND INSPECTING CAM SHAFT

frames.name: p079-text-0535
frames.text: Figure 33 illustrates one of these units.

frames.name: p079-text-0536
frames.text: The following instructions apply to each of them.

frames.name: p079-text-0537
frames.text: The housing assemblies should be dismounted from the engine in

frames.name: p079-text-0538
frames.text: the following manner:

frames.name: p079-text-0539
frames.text: 1. Disconnect oil pipe by unscrewing nut No. 8122.

frames.name: p079-text-0540
frames.text: The connection No. 812 may then be slipped off. Put the two

frames.name: p079-text-0541
frames.text: gaskets, No. 157, back in place and screw on the nut, No. 8122.

frames.name: p079-text-0542
frames.text: 2. Unscrew the packing nut No. 8066 and slide it and the felt-

frames.name: p079-text-0543
frames.text: packing washing No. 8068 up on the housing. If the felt washer does

frames.name: p079-text-0544
frames.text: not fit sufficiently tight to hold both in place, tie them so that they

frames.name: p079-text-0545
frames.text: will not slip off.

frames.name: p079-text-0546
frames.text: 3. Remove 12 nuts No. 102 and washers No. 112 and lay them to

frames.name: p079-text-0547
frames.text: one side in the order in which they were originally assembled.

frames.name: p079-text-0548
frames.text: 4. The unit may now be lifted off the engine. Raise it carefully and

frames.name: p079-text-0549
frames.text: evenly so as to avoid risk of bending the studs.

frames.name: p079-text-0550
frames.text: 5. Put the washers No. 112 and the nuts No. 102 back in place on

frames.name: p079-text-0551
frames.text: their proper studs.

frames.name: p079-text-0552
frames.text: 6. Examine all rocker lever shafts with respect to the fit in bearings.

frames.name: p079-text-0553
frames.text: These shafts should have from 0.005 to 0.010 end play and from

frames.name: p079-text-0554
frames.text: 0.001 to 0.0015 clearance in bearings. The bearing fit should be

frames.name: p079-text-0555
frames.text: “free running” and the radial clearance or shake should be barely

frames.name: p079-text-0556
frames.text: perceptible.

frames.name: p079-text-0557
frames.text: 7. Remove cam-shaft housing cover bolts No. 178, washers No. 112,

frames.name: p079-text-0558
frames.text: and covers No. 8095 and lay them to one side in the order in which

frames.name: p079-text-0559
frames.text: they were originally assembled.

frames.name: p079-text-0560
frames.text: Caution.—The joints between the covers and housing are “lapped”

frames.name: p079-text-0561
frames.text: and the covers are marked to fit in their proper place. Care must be

frames.name: p079-text-0562
frames.text: exercised in handling these parts so as to avoid marring the surfaces

frames.name: p079-text-0563
frames.text: which come in contact.

frames.name: p079-text-0564
frames.text: 8. Examine rocker levers. As each tappet has been adjusted as to

frames.name: p079-text-0565
frames.text: clearance for the particular valve which it operates, the rocker levers

frames.name: p079-text-0566
frames.text: should be laid to one side in the order in which they were originally

frames.name: p079-text-0567
frames.text: assembled.

frames.name: p079-text-0568
frames.text: 9. Examine the tappets to see that they are tight and that the faces

frames.name: p079-text-0569
frames.text: do not show undue wear.

frames.name: p079-text-0570
frames.text: 10. Examine the rollers to see that they are not cracked. See that

frames.name: p079-text-0571
frames.text: the rollers are free running and show no flat spots. The bearing for

frames.name: p079-text-0572
frames.text: the rollers is a steel thimble which is a free fit in the roller. This

frames.name: p079-text-0573
frames.text: thimble is pinched tight in the rocker lever fork by the pin No. 8083,

frames.name: p079-text-0574
frames.text: which is riveted at assembly in rocker lever. The permissible shake

frames.name: p079-text-0575
frames.text: is 0.001. Roller should have 0.010 side play in the fork of the rocker

frames.name: p079-text-0576
frames.text: lever.

frames.name: p080-text-0578
frames.text: 11. Examine rocker lever bearings. See that they are clean and

frames.name: p080-text-0579
frames.text: show no evidences of “scoring.” Scored shafts should be smoothed

frames.name: p080-text-0580
frames.text: up with a fine file and sandpaper. Bearings should be touched up

frames.name: p080-text-0581
frames.text: with a scraper.

frames.name: p080-text-0582
frames.text: 12. Remove cam shaft. Take out seven cam-shaft bearing lock

frames.name: p080-text-0583
frames.text: screws No. 8108 with their gaskets, No. 157. This will permit the

frames.name: p080-text-0584
frames.text: cam shaft and six bearings to be withdrawn through the gear end of

frames.name: p080-text-0585
frames.text: the housing. The bearing No. 12250 may be pushed out through the

frames.name: p080-text-0586
frames.text: other end of the housing. The cam shaft bearings are so fitted that

frames.name: p080-text-0587
frames.text: they should come out easily. Should they stick the four screws No.

frames.name: p080-text-0588
frames.text: 8219 and bearing cover plate No. 8376 may be removed and the

frames.name: p080-text-0589
frames.text: shaft driven out with a soft plate.

frames.name: p080-text-0590
frames.text: 13. Examine cam-shaft bearings. These bearings should have a

frames.name: p080-text-0591
frames.text: clearance on the shaft of from 0.001 to 0.003, which means that the

frames.name: p080-text-0592
frames.text: “shake” will be just perceptible with an oil film in the bearing.

frames.name: p080-text-0593
frames.text: The gear end bearings should have an end play of from 0.001 to

frames.name: p080-text-0594
frames.text: 0.003 between the cam-shaft flanges. All bearings should be clean

frames.name: p080-text-0595
frames.text: and free from “scores.” The sets of cam-shaft bearings are

frames.name: p080-text-0596
frames.text: “stepped.” That is, the bearing at the gear end has the greatest

frames.name: p080-text-0597
frames.text: outside diameter. The next one is

frames.name: p080-text-0601
frames.text: inch smaller; the third bearing

frames.name: p080-text-0602
frames.text: is

frames.name: p080-text-0606
frames.text: inch smaller than the second, etc. Therefore, to facilitate reas-

frames.name: p080-text-0607
frames.text: sembling, lay the bearings out in the order in which they are dis-

frames.name: p080-text-0608
frames.text: assembled.

frames.name: p080-text-0609
frames.text: 14. Examine cam shaft. See that all bearing surfaces are bright

frames.name: p080-text-0610
frames.text: and smooth. Inspect it from the shaft carefully for cracks and soft

frames.name: p080-text-0611
frames.text: spots.

frames.name: p080-text-0612
frames.text: 15. Examine cam-shaft gear. See that the teeth are all intact and

frames.name: p080-text-0613
frames.text: do not show undue wear. Unless the gear is defective it should not

frames.name: p080-text-0614
frames.text: be necessary to remove it from the shaft.

frames.name: p080-text-0615
frames.text: 16. Remove cam-shaft upper drive shaft. Take off nuts No. 101

frames.name: p080-text-0616
frames.text: and washers No. 111, which will permit the removal of housing No.

frames.name: p080-text-0617
frames.text: 8109. A gasket No. 8139,

frames.name: p080-text-0621
frames.text: inch thick, will be found between the

frames.name: p080-text-0622
frames.text: flange of No. 8109 and the cam-shaft housing.

frames.name: p080-text-0623
frames.text: 17. Withdraw the drive shaft and examine the bearing surfaces

frames.name: p080-text-0624
frames.text: and the bushings in which they run. See that the gear is tight on

frames.name: p080-text-0625
frames.text: the shaft and that neither the gear not the splines at the lower end

frames.name: p080-text-0626
frames.text: of the shaft show undue wear. Should it be necessary to change

frames.name: p080-text-0627
frames.text: either of the cam-shaft drive shaft bearings, the new bushings should

frames.name: p080-text-0628
frames.text: be oiled on the outside and pressed in carefully under an arbor press

frames.name: p080-text-0629
frames.text: or in a vise. They should then be reamed to size—the upper one,

frames.name: p080-text-0630
frames.text: No. 8107, to 0.875-0.0005, and the lower one, No. 8092, to 1.125-

frames.name: p080-text-0632
frames.text: All parts should be washed in gasoline or kerosene and blown off

frames.name: p080-text-0633
frames.text: with an air jet.

frames.name: p080-text-0634
frames.text: Especial care should be taken that all oil passages are clear and

frames.name: p080-text-0635
frames.text: free from dirt.

frames.name: p081-text-0002
frames.text: ASSEMBLING THE CAM SHAFT

frames.name: p081-text-0003
frames.text: 1. Fit the cam shafts with their bearings in the cam-shaft hous-

frames.name: p081-text-0004
frames.text: ings. If it has been found necessary to replace any of the bearings

frames.name: p081-text-0005
frames.text: the new ones should be tried in their proper places in the housings

frames.name: p081-text-0006
frames.text: to see that they are what is termed a “wringing” fit. That is, they

frames.name: p081-text-0007
frames.text: should be free enough so that they may be turned with a drift to

frames.name: p081-text-0008
frames.text: line up the lock screw hole and still there should be no “shake” per-

frames.name: p081-text-0009
frames.text: ceptible. If a new shaft is to be fitted all bearings should be tried in

frames.name: p081-text-0010
frames.text: their proper places on the shaft. The diametrical clearance should

frames.name: p081-text-0011
frames.text: be from 0.001 to 0.003. Oil all bearing surfaces with clean oil before

frames.name: p081-text-0012
frames.text: assembling. Be sure that punched holes in gasket No. 8379 and end

frames.name: p081-text-0013
frames.text: plate No. 8376 line up with oil hole in bearing No. 12250, and that

frames.name: p081-text-0014
frames.text: screws are wired. Line up the lack screw holes carefully and put the

frames.name: p081-text-0015
frames.text: screws in place with their gaskets.

frames.name: p081-text-0016
frames.text: If a new shaft or new gear is to be fitted be sure that cam-shaft

frames.name: p081-text-0017
frames.text: gear bolts No. 171 are in place before putting on bearing No. 8111

frames.name: p081-text-0018
frames.text: and No. 8112. In the above case leave the gear off until later on in

frames.name: p081-text-0019
frames.text: the process of assembling the engine. (See “Timing Valves,” p. 106.)

frames.name: p081-text-0020
frames.text: 2. Put the rocker levers and housing covers in place and test each

frames.name: p081-text-0021
frames.text: lever for free operation.

frames.name: p081-text-0022
frames.text: 3. Screw on the cover No. 8088 against its gasket, No. 169.

frames.name: p081-text-0023
frames.text: 4. Put the cam-shaft drive (upper) and its housing in place with

frames.name: p081-text-0024
frames.text: the gasket No. 8139 between the flanges. The shaft should turn

frames.name: p081-text-0025
frames.text: freely after the housing bolts are drawn up and the end play should

frames.name: p081-text-0026
frames.text: not exceed 0.008 inch. If the original gears are used they should be

frames.name: p081-text-0027
frames.text: meshed so that the marks come in line.

frames.name: p081-text-0028
frames.text: Permissible “back lash” in these gears is 0.005 inch to 0.010 inch.

frames.name: p081-text-0029
frames.text: LOWER CAM-SHAFT DRIVE SHAFTS

frames.name: p081-text-0030
frames.text: These assemblies, No. 8208, are illustrated on page 56, and each

frames.name: p081-text-0031
frames.text: embodies the parts in list below.

frames.name: p081-text-0032
frames.text: Take off four nuts No. 101, which will release the cover No. 8072

frames.name: p081-text-0033
frames.text: and permit the assembly to be lifted out.

frames.name: p081-text-0034
frames.text: Examine gear and splined socket. Try end play in bearings. It

frames.name: p081-text-0035
frames.text: should not exceed 0.004 inch.

frames.name: p081-text-0036
frames.text: TO DISASSEMBLE CAM-SHAFT DRIVE

frames.name: p081-text-0037
frames.text: Remove nut No. 8142 and draw off gear with gear puller.

frames.name: p081-text-0038
frames.text: Caution.—Do not attempt to drive shaft out through gear.

frames.name: p081-text-0039
frames.text: The keys in shaft will not pass through the lower ball bearing.

frames.name: p081-text-0040
frames.text: After drawing off the gear the keys may be lifted out and the shaft

frames.name: p081-text-0041
frames.text: may then be tapped or pressed out through the bearings and spacer.

frames.name: p081-text-0042
frames.text: The parts of this unit should be assembled in the reverse order to

frames.name: p081-text-0043
frames.text: the above, care being taken that the keys are properly seated in the

frames.name: p081-text-0044
frames.text: shaft and that all parts are drawn up snugly by means of the nut

frames.name: p081-text-0046
frames.text: Note.—Unless some part of this assembly is defective it is not
frames.pdf_text: NOTE.—Unless some part of this assembly is defective it is not

frames.name: p081-text-0047
frames.text: advisable to take it apart.

frames.name: p082-text-0049
frames.text: Plate No. 51

frames.name: p082-text-0050
frames.text: GENERATOR DRIVE SHAFT

frames.name: p083-text-0052
frames.text: DISASSEMBLING GENERATOR DRIVE

frames.name: p083-text-0053
frames.text: Remove flat-head screw No. 214. This will permit the generator

frames.name: p083-text-0054
frames.text: drive-shaft assembly No. 8210 to be lifted out. One or more metal

frames.name: p083-text-0055
frames.text: shims 0.002 inch thick will be found between the bearing container

frames.name: p083-text-0056
frames.text: No. 8154 and the crank case. The number of shims will be sufficient

frames.name: p083-text-0057
frames.text: to insure the proper mesh of the lower generator drive-shaft gear

frames.name: p083-text-0058
frames.text: with the crank-shaft gear. They should be tied together and hung

frames.name: p083-text-0059
frames.text: up or laid to one side so that they will not be lost or damaged. Ex-

frames.name: p083-text-0060
frames.text: amine gears for wear. End play in bearings should not exceed 0.004

frames.name: p083-text-0061
frames.text: inch. Remove nuts No. 8151.

frames.name: p083-text-0062
frames.text: Do not attempt to drive shaft out, but draw off gear No. 8074

frames.name: p083-text-0063
frames.text: with a gear puller. The same construction is employed here as in

frames.name: p083-text-0064
frames.text: the lower cam-shaft drive assembly and the same caution applies.

frames.name: p083-text-0065
frames.text: Remove keys No. 160 and draw off spacer and bearing assembly

frames.name: p083-text-0067
frames.text: Remove gear No. 8080 and keys No. 160, which will permit the

frames.name: p083-text-0068
frames.text: spacer No. 8149 and bearing No. 8060 to be taken off.

frames.name: p083-text-0069
frames.text: The bearing No. 8060 is held in place in the container No. 8154

frames.name: p083-text-0070
frames.text: by means of the lock ring No. 8524. If it should be found necessary

frames.name: p083-text-0071
frames.text: to remove this bearing the lock ring may be compressed with a pair

frames.name: p083-text-0072
frames.text: of round-nosed pliers.

frames.name: p083-text-0073
frames.text: The parts of this unit should be assembled in the reverse order to

frames.name: p083-text-0074
frames.text: the above, care being taken that the keys are properly seated in the

frames.name: p083-text-0075
frames.text: shaft and that all parts are drawn up snugly by means of the unit

frames.name: p083-text-0077
frames.text: Note.—Unless some part of this assembly is defective it is not
frames.pdf_text: NOTE.—Unless some part of this assembly is defective it is not

frames.name: p083-text-0078
frames.text: advisable to take it apart, as it has been carefully inspected as to

frames.name: p083-text-0079
frames.text: proper alignment of gear teeth.

frames.name: p083-text-0080
frames.text: OILING SYSTEM

frames.name: p083-text-0081
frames.text: GENERAL DESCRIPTION

frames.name: p083-text-0082
frames.text: The oil supply is carried in a reservoir provided with a suitable

frames.name: p083-text-0083
frames.text: means for cooling it. Oil is led from this reservoir to the connection

frames.name: p083-text-0084
frames.text: on the right side of the oil-pump body marked “oil in.” It is filtered

frames.name: p083-text-0085
frames.text: at this point through a large area fine mesh screen. A delivery pump

frames.name: p083-text-0086
frames.text: of the gear type takes the oil up after it has passed through the screen

frames.name: p083-text-0087
frames.text: and delivers it under considerable pressure to a distributor pipe

frames.name: p083-text-0088
frames.text: running the entire length of the crank case. Opening out of the

frames.name: p083-text-0089
frames.text: passage between the pump and the distributor pipe is a pressure

frames.name: p083-text-0090
frames.text: regulating valve designed to maintain a pressure not to exceed 50

frames.name: p083-text-0091
frames.text: pounds per square inch on the oiling system.

frames.name: p083-text-0092
frames.text: Pipes are fitted in the case leading from the distributor pipe to

frames.name: p083-text-0093
frames.text: the main crank-shaft bushings.

frames.name: p084-text-0095
frames.text: The crank shaft is hollow and in the center of each main bearing a

frames.name: p084-text-0096
frames.text: radial hole is drilled through the shaft into the hollow center. This

frames.name: p084-text-0097
frames.text: hole in the shaft registers with the corresponding hole in the bearing

frames.name: p084-text-0098
frames.text: bushing once every revolution of the shaft, at which time a small

frames.name: p084-text-0099
frames.text: quantity of oil is forced through into the hollow crank shaft. A

frames.name: p084-text-0100
frames.text: passage leads from each hollow main bearing to the adjacent crank

frames.name: p084-text-0101
frames.text: pin, which is also hollow. A radial hole is also drilled through each

frames.name: p084-text-0102
frames.text: crank pin and carries the oil out on the surface of the pin. Oil

frames.name: p084-text-0103
frames.text: grooves and passages in the connecting-rod bushings insure proper

frames.name: p084-text-0104
frames.text: lubrication for both the forked and plain connecting rods.

frames.name: p084-text-0105
frames.text: The excess oil thrown off the rapidly moving connecting-rod ends

frames.name: p084-text-0106
frames.text: forms a mist which lubricates the piston pins and the cylinder

frames.name: p084-text-0107
frames.text: walls.

frames.name: p084-text-0108
frames.text: Part of the oil conducted to the main crank-shaft bearing at the

frames.name: p084-text-0109
frames.text: propeller end of the engine goes through a passage around this bearing

frames.name: p084-text-0110
frames.text: and up through pipes to the propeller end of the cam-shaft housings.

frames.name: p084-text-0111
frames.text: From the end of the cam-shaft housings it is led around the end cam-

frames.name: p084-text-0112
frames.text: shaft bearing to a passage drilled diametrically through the bearing

frames.name: p084-text-0113
frames.text: midway of its length. Once every revolution of the cam shaft a

frames.name: p084-text-0114
frames.text: hole drilled through the cam shaft into its hollow center registers

frames.name: p084-text-0115
frames.text: with the oil passage through the bearing.

frames.name: p084-text-0116
frames.text: Thus once every revolution a small quantity of oil is forced into

frames.name: p084-text-0117
frames.text: the hollow cam shaft.

frames.name: p084-text-0118
frames.text: The oil is led through the cam shaft and out through holes drilled

frames.name: p084-text-0119
frames.text: in it to each cam-shaft bearing. The excess works out of the ends

frames.name: p084-text-0120
frames.text: of these bearings and collects in small reservoirs to a depth of about

frames.name: p084-text-0121
frames.text: ¼ inch. The cams, in revolving, dip into this oil and splash it over

frames.name: p084-text-0122
frames.text: the cam rollers and into pockets in the rocker lever shafts. From

frames.name: p084-text-0123
frames.text: these pockets it is led through the hollow rocker shafts to the rocker-

frames.name: p084-text-0124
frames.text: shaft bearings.

frames.name: p084-text-0125
frames.text: The excess oil eventually finds its way to the gear end of the cam-

frames.name: p084-text-0126
frames.text: shaft housings, over the gears and down the drive-shaft housing into a

frames.name: p084-text-0127
frames.text: chamber just above the oil pump.

frames.name: p084-text-0128
frames.text: The excess oil thrown off in the crank case by the connecting

frames.name: p084-text-0129
frames.text: rods collects in this same chamber when the engine is inclined so

frames.name: p084-text-0130
frames.text: that the propeller end is high. If the propeller end of the engine is

frames.name: p084-text-0131
frames.text: low, this oil collects in a small sump or chamber at the propeller end

frames.name: p084-text-0132
frames.text: of the crank case.

frames.name: p084-text-0133
frames.text: Immediately above the oil delivery pump is located an oil-return

frames.name: p084-text-0134
frames.text: pump, consisting of three gears, and driven by the same shaft as the

frames.name: p084-text-0135
frames.text: delivery pump. The function of this oil-return pump is to draw the

frames.name: p084-text-0136
frames.text: excess oil out of the crank case and return it to the oil reservoir.

frames.name: p084-text-0137
frames.text: One half of this sump draws oil from the sump at the propeller end

frames.name: p084-text-0138
frames.text: of the crank case and the other half draws oil from the sump at the

frames.name: p085-text-0140
frames.text: Plate No. 52

frames.name: p085-text-0141
frames.text: WATER PUMP ASSEMBLY

frames.name: p086-text-0143
frames.text: distributer end of the crank case. Both halves of the pump deliver

frames.name: p086-text-0144
frames.text: oil to the connection on the left side of the oil-pump body marked

frames.name: p086-text-0145
frames.text: “oil out,” from which point it returns to the oil reservoir.

frames.name: p086-text-0146
frames.text: OIL PUMP

frames.name: p086-text-0147
frames.text: The oil-pump assembly No. 8200 embodies the parts enumerated

frames.name: p086-text-0148
frames.text: in the list at the end of this chapter.

frames.name: p086-text-0149
frames.text: DISASSEMBLING AND INSPECTION

frames.name: p086-text-0150
frames.text: Dismount the oil-pump assembly from the engine by removing nuts

frames.name: p086-text-0151
frames.text: No. 101 and washers No. 111. Then:

frames.name: p086-text-0152
frames.text: 1. Take out bolts No. 116, nuts No. 101, and washers No. 111.

frames.name: p086-text-0153
frames.text: This will permit the cover No. 8381 of the oil-pump body to be taken

frames.name: p086-text-0154
frames.text: off, and will release the oil strainer No. 8220.

frames.name: p086-text-0155
frames.text: 2. Withdraw the oil-pump shaft No. 8148. Examine the splined

frames.name: p086-text-0156
frames.text: ends of this shaft to see that they do not show excessive wear.

frames.name: p086-text-0157
frames.text: 3. Bend down the ears of the nut lock No. 8636 and remove the

frames.name: p086-text-0158
frames.text: nut No. 8535. This will permit the withdrawal of the upper oil-

frames.name: p086-text-0159
frames.text: pump screen.

frames.name: p086-text-0160
frames.text: 4. Remove four bolts No. 118, which will permit the upper half

frames.name: p086-text-0161
frames.text: of the oil-pump body No. 8189 to be removed. This will expose

frames.name: p086-text-0162
frames.text: two driven gears No. 8177 and a driving gear No. 8187. These gears

frames.name: p086-text-0163
frames.text: should be examined as to their fit in the housing. This can best be

frames.name: p086-text-0164
frames.text: tested by inserting the drive shaft through its bearing in the housing

frames.name: p086-text-0165
frames.text: and laying the gears in the housing in their proper position, with

frames.name: p086-text-0166
frames.text: their bearing pins No. 8179 and No. 8383 in place. The diametrical

frames.name: p086-text-0167
frames.text: clearance of the gears in the housing should not exceed 0.004 inch.

frames.name: p086-text-0168
frames.text: The permissible end play of the gears in the housing is 0.003 inch.

frames.name: p086-text-0169
frames.text: 5. Lift the separating plate No. 8188. This exposes gears No. 8178

frames.name: p086-text-0170
frames.text: and No. 8186. These also should be examined as to fit in the housing.

frames.name: p086-text-0171
frames.text: The above clearances apply to these gears.

frames.name: p086-text-0172
frames.text: 6. The pressure relief valve may be unscrewed and the valve

frames.name: p086-text-0173
frames.text: No. 8192 and seat No. 8368 should be examined.

frames.name: p086-text-0174
frames.text: ASSEMBLING

frames.name: p086-text-0175
frames.text: The parts should all be washed carefully and assembled in the

frames.name: p086-text-0176
frames.text: following order:

frames.name: p086-text-0177
frames.text: (a) The driving gear No. 8186 and the driven gear No. 8178 on its

frames.name: p086-text-0178
frames.text: pin No. 8383.

frames.name: p086-text-0179
frames.text: (b) The separating plate No. 8188.

frames.name: p086-text-0180
frames.text: (c) The driven gears No. 8177 and their pins, and the driving gear

frames.name: p086-text-0182
frames.text: (d) The oil-pump body upper half No. 8189.

frames.name: p086-text-0183
frames.text: Note.—This part of the oil-pump housing is located in its proper
frames.pdf_text: NOTE.—This part of the oil-pump housing is located in its proper

frames.name: p086-text-0184
frames.text: position by means of two dowel pins No. 174. Care should be taken

frames.name: p086-text-0185
frames.text: that these pins are in their proper places.

frames.name: p087-text-0187
frames.text: (e) The four bolts No. 118, with their washers and nuts, may be

frames.name: p087-text-0188
frames.text: put in place and tightened up and three of the bolts cottered.

frames.name: p087-text-0189
frames.text: (f) The pressure relief valve may now be screwed in against its

frames.name: p087-text-0190
frames.text: seat No. 8368. Lock wire should be passed through the relief valve

frames.name: p087-text-0191
frames.text: cage and through the bolt No. 118, which was not cottered.

frames.name: p087-text-0192
frames.text: (g) Especial care should be taken that the strainer No. 8230 is

frames.name: p087-text-0193
frames.text: thoroughly cleaned. It may now be put in place and the cover

frames.name: p087-text-0194
frames.text: No. 8381 bolted on. The gasket No. 8382, between the oil-pump

frames.name: p087-text-0195
frames.text: body and its cover plate, should be replaced if it has been damaged

frames.name: p087-text-0196
frames.text: in any way in disassembling.

frames.name: p087-text-0197
frames.text: (h) Clean the upper screen and put it in place. It will be advis-

frames.name: p087-text-0198
frames.text: able to install a new nut lock No. 8536, which may be bent up to

frames.name: p087-text-0199
frames.text: lock the nut No. 8535 after it has been properly screwed down.
