frames.name: p087-text-0200
frames.text: CYLINDER ASSEMBLY

frames.name: p087-text-0201
frames.text: Cylinder and valve assemblies may be dismounted by removing

frames.name: p087-text-0202
frames.text: the nuts No. 103 and special nuts No. 8224. Cylinder should be

frames.name: p087-text-0203
frames.text: lifted off carefully and the pistons, when released, should not be

frames.name: p087-text-0204
frames.text: allowed to fall over against the sides of the crank case. After remov-

frames.name: p087-text-0205
frames.text: ing the cylinder the nuts should be put back on the studs and screwed

frames.name: p087-text-0206
frames.text: on just far enough to prevent them from being lost. This will not

frames.name: p087-text-0207
frames.text: only protect the studs, but will prevent confusion in reassembling.

frames.name: p087-text-0208
frames.text: If some old pieces of hose are available, short sections should be

frames.name: p087-text-0209
frames.text: slipped over two studs on opposite sides of each cylinder opening

frames.name: p087-text-0210
frames.text: as shown above.

frames.name: p087-text-0211
frames.text: VALVES

frames.name: p087-text-0212
frames.text: TO REMOVE VALVES

frames.name: p087-text-0213
frames.text: To do this the valves must be held up against their seats and the

frames.name: p087-text-0214
frames.text: springs compressed sufficiently by means of a valve-spring compressor

frames.name: p087-text-0215
frames.text: Plate No. 53

frames.name: p087-text-0216
frames.text: CYLINDER ASSEMBLY

frames.name: p088-text-0218
frames.text: supplied in the tool kit to permit the lower collar being moved down

frames.name: p088-text-0219
frames.text: far enough to uncover the valve-spring collar keys. These keys (two

frames.name: p088-text-0220
frames.text: parts) may now be lifted out and the springs and valves removed.

frames.name: p088-text-0221
frames.text: The same inside spring is used on both intake and exhaust valves.

frames.name: p088-text-0222
frames.text: The outside spring may be identified by the fact that the exhaust-

frames.name: p088-text-0223
frames.text: valve spring has 10 coils while the inlet valve spring has 12 coils.

frames.name: p088-text-0224
frames.text: Also the exhaust-valve spring exerts a pressure of 45 pounds when

frames.name: p088-text-0225
frames.text: compressed to a length of 2¼ inches, and the intake-valve spring

frames.name: p088-text-0226
frames.text: exerts a pressure of 23½ pounds when compressed to a length of 2¼

frames.name: p088-text-0227
frames.text: inches. The valves for each cylinder have the cylinder serial num-

frames.name: p088-text-0228
frames.text: ber etched on them and are marked “ex” (exhaust) and “in” (inlet),

frames.name: p088-text-0229
frames.text: respectively.

frames.name: p088-text-0230
frames.text: CLEAN VALVES

frames.name: p088-text-0231
frames.text: Clean the valves carefully, and if the valve stems are gummed up

frames.name: p088-text-0232
frames.text: with burned oil they should be dressed down with fine sandpaper.

frames.name: p088-text-0233
frames.text: Examine the valve seats in the cylinder and the face of the valves

frames.name: p088-text-0234
frames.text: which comes in contact with these seats.

frames.name: p088-text-0235
frames.text: The valves should be tested for gas tightness. This can best be

frames.name: p088-text-0236
frames.text: done by inverting the cylinder, with the valves in place, and pouring

frames.name: p088-text-0237
frames.text: a small quantity of gasoline in the cylinder. Watch for seepage

frames.name: p088-text-0238
frames.text: around the valve. If the valves show any leak they should be care-

frames.name: p088-text-0239
frames.text: fully ground in. The cylinder for this operation, should be held in

frames.name: p088-text-0240
frames.text: position by means of the flange at the bottom. An arrangement for

frames.name: p088-text-0241
frames.text: holding the cylinder for valve grinding can be readily made.

frames.name: p088-text-0242
frames.text: Note that in this illustration a light spring is inserted under the

frames.name: p088-text-0243
frames.text: valves to partially counterbalance the weight of the tool by means of

frames.name: p088-text-0244
frames.text: which the valve is turned. An efficient valve-grinding tool will be

frames.name: p088-text-0245
frames.text: found in the tool kit. In grinding the valve it should not be revolved

frames.name: p088-text-0246
frames.text: but should be rocked backward and forward, and frequently lifted

frames.name: p088-text-0247
frames.text: off its seat and its position on the seat changed in order to distribute

frames.name: p088-text-0248
frames.text: the abrasive evenly and to prevent “scoring” the valve. Valves

frames.name: p088-text-0249
frames.text: should not be ground any oftener than is absolutely necessary, and

frames.name: p088-text-0250
frames.text: then only enough to “clean up” the seat. If a valve is pitted or

frames.name: p088-text-0251
frames.text: warped to such an extent that it is necessary to grind it heavily, care

frames.name: p088-text-0252
frames.text: should be taken that any ridge or shoulder formed on the edge of the

frames.name: p088-text-0253
frames.text: valve seat be dressed down with a fine mill file. The abrasive should

frames.name: p088-text-0254
frames.text: be carefully washed off the valve, the seat, and the inside of the cyl-

frames.name: p088-text-0255
frames.text: inder. Test seating of valve with Prussian blue.

frames.name: p088-text-0256
frames.text: Any valves which are badly warped should be replaced and the

frames.name: p088-text-0257
frames.text: valve seat in the cylinder should be trued up with a valve seat reamer

frames.name: p088-text-0258
frames.text: before grinding in the new valve.

frames.name: p088-text-0259
frames.text: Replace the valves, the lower collars, the springs, the upper collars,

frames.name: p088-text-0260
frames.text: and the collar keys.

frames.name: p089-text-0262
frames.text: PISTONS

frames.name: p089-text-0263
frames.text: DISMOUNTING THE PISTONS

frames.name: p089-text-0264
frames.text: Remove the piston-pin retain-

frames.name: p089-text-0265
frames.text: ers by either one of the methods

frames.name: p089-text-0266
frames.text: shown herewith. Press out the

frames.name: p089-text-0267
frames.text: piston pins with a brass drift sup-

frames.name: p089-text-0268
frames.text: plied in the tool kit. The fit of

frames.name: p089-text-0269
frames.text: the piston pin in the piston should

frames.name: p089-text-0270
frames.text: be from a free running fit without

frames.name: p089-text-0271
frames.text: play to a light drive fit. It is pre-

frames.name: p089-text-0272
frames.text: ferable to have the piston pin a free

frames.name: p089-text-0273
frames.text: fit in the piston than to have it drive out hard.

frames.name: p089-text-0274
frames.text: Clean the carbon deposit off from the piston head both on the top

frames.name: p089-text-0275
frames.text: and on the under side. The polished surface of the top of the piston

frames.name: p089-text-0276
frames.text: head should not be marred or scratched if it can be avoided.

frames.name: p089-text-0277
frames.text: Examine the piston for scores. It is very likely that the pistons

frames.name: p089-text-0278
frames.text: will show scratches which were caused during the first run in of the

frames.name: p089-text-0279
frames.text: engine. It is difficult to draw a line of distinction between what is

frames.name: p089-text-0280
frames.text: termed a scratch and a score. A piston should not be discarded unless

frames.name: p089-text-0281
frames.text: the scores extend part of the piston rings and seem to be of recent

frames.name: p089-text-0282
frames.text: origin.

frames.name: p089-text-0283
frames.text: Examine the piston for even bearing on its outside surface. If any

frames.name: p089-text-0284
frames.text: piston shows excessive wear on one side, at the bottom and not at the

frames.name: p089-text-0285
frames.text: top, it is an indication that the connecting rod is twisted or bent.

frames.name: p089-text-0286
frames.text: RINGS

frames.name: p089-text-0287
frames.text: Examine the piston ring

frames.name: p089-text-0288
frames.text: for even bearing on the out-

frames.name: p089-text-0289
frames.text: side surfaces. The rings

frames.name: p089-text-0290
frames.text: should be a free fit in the

frames.name: p089-text-0291
frames.text: grooves, and should not be so

frames.name: p089-text-0292
frames.text: loose that any shake is notice-

frames.name: p089-text-0293
frames.text: able.

frames.name: p089-text-0294
frames.text: Inspect condition of ring

frames.name: p089-text-0295
frames.text: grooves through the gap as to

frames.name: p089-text-0296
frames.text: carbon deposit. If the carbon

frames.name: p089-text-0297
frames.text: is soft and not of great amount

frames.name: p089-text-0298
frames.text: it may be wiped out with a

frames.name: p089-text-0299
frames.text: soft rag over a splinter of

frames.name: p089-text-0300
frames.text: wood inserted through the

frames.name: p089-text-0301
frames.text: gap in the ring. If the

frames.name: p089-text-0302
frames.text: amount of carbon is excessive,

frames.name: p089-text-0303
frames.text: and caked exceptionally hard the ring should always be taken off.

frames.name: p089-text-0304
frames.text: Plate No. 54

frames.name: p089-text-0305
frames.text: Plate No. 55

frames.name: p089-text-0306
frames.text: REMOVING PISTON PIN

frames.name: p089-text-0307
frames.text: REMOVING PIN (ALTERNATIVE METHOD)

frames.name: p090-text-0309
frames.text: Extreme care should be exercised in removing the rings. They

frames.name: p090-text-0310
frames.text: should not be expanded more than is absolutely necessary to pass

frames.name: p090-text-0311
frames.text: them over the top of the piston. As the piston material is com-

frames.name: p090-text-0312
frames.text: paratively soft, care should be taken not to mar or scratch its

frames.name: p090-text-0313
frames.text: outside surface.

frames.name: p090-text-0314
frames.text: Ring grooves should be wiped out with a soft cloth moistened with

frames.name: p090-text-0315
frames.text: gasoline, and any carbon caked in these grooves may be scraped out

frames.name: p090-text-0316
frames.text: with a piece of wood.

frames.name: p090-text-0317
frames.text: It is preferable to put back the old rings if the wear has not been

frames.name: p090-text-0318
frames.text: too excessive than to fit new rings which have not been run in.

frames.name: p090-text-0319
frames.text: In refitting the rings in the grooves the same care should be exer-

frames.name: p090-text-0320
frames.text: cised as in removing them, in order that the piston surface may not

frames.name: p090-text-0321
frames.text: be scratched or marred. The gap between the ends of the ring

frames.name: p090-text-0322
frames.text: should be not less than 0.025 inch when the ring is fitted in the cyl-

frames.name: p090-text-0323
frames.text: inder.

frames.name: p090-text-0324
frames.text: The pistons are marked as to their location in the engine 1L,

frames.name: p090-text-0325
frames.text: 1R, etc. These marks are stamped in the depression on the side

frames.name: p090-text-0326
frames.text: of the piston. In reassembling pistons on rods, the marked side

frames.name: p090-text-0327
frames.text: should be toward the distributor end of the engine. The number

frames.name: p090-text-0328
frames.text: of ounces which each piston weighs over 3 pounds is also stamped

frames.name: p090-text-0329
frames.text: in this depression.

frames.name: p090-text-0330
frames.text: If it was found necessary to replace any pistons, new ones of

frames.name: p090-text-0331
frames.text: exactly the same weight should be selected from the stock.

frames.name: p090-text-0332
frames.text: Caution.—Great care should be exercised in handling pistons to

frames.name: p090-text-0333
frames.text: prevent them from being subjected to any sort of rough usage which

frames.name: p090-text-0334
frames.text: would be likely to spring them “out of

frames.name: p090-text-0335
frames.text: round.”

frames.name: p090-text-0336
frames.text: Do not allow piston with rings to slip by

frames.name: p090-text-0337
frames.text: the counter bore at the top of the cylinder.

frames.name: p090-text-0338
frames.text: It is almost impossible to compress the

frames.name: p090-text-0339
frames.text: rings enough to push the piston down again

frames.name: p090-text-0340
frames.text: without damaging the surface of the piston

frames.name: p090-text-0341
frames.text: or the cylinder wall.

frames.name: p090-text-0342
frames.text: To apply or remove piston rings, use hack-

frames.name: p090-text-0343
frames.text: saw blades with the teeth ground off and the

frames.name: p090-text-0344
frames.text: sharp edges rounded.

frames.name: p090-text-0345
frames.text: The bearing surface on the piston here illus-

frames.name: p090-text-0346
frames.text: trated indicates a bent or twisted connecting

frames.name: p090-text-0347
frames.text: rod. Note that the heaviest bearing is at

frames.name: p090-text-0348
frames.text: the top right and bottom left. The scores

frames.name: p090-text-0349
frames.text: are characteristic of aluminum pistons. The

frames.name: p090-text-0350
frames.text: piston shown should not be condemned on

frames.name: p090-text-0351
frames.text: account of these scores.

frames.name: p090-text-0352
frames.text: Plate No. 56

frames.name: p090-text-0353
frames.text: FITTING RINGS

frames.name: p091-text-0355
frames.text: CONNECTING RODS

frames.name: p091-text-0356
frames.text: DISASSEMBLING AND INSPECTION

frames.name: p091-text-0357
frames.text: 1. After the pistons are all removed, take off nuts No. 105.

frames.name: p091-text-0358
frames.text: 2. Turn the crank case bottom side up and take out the small

frames.name: p091-text-0359
frames.text: bolts No. 116 which fasten the two halves of the crank case together.

frames.name: p091-text-0360
frames.text: 3. Lift off the bottom half of the crank case, being careful to raise

frames.name: p091-text-0361
frames.text: it steadily and evenly so as not to spring or bend the crank-shaft

frames.name: p091-text-0362
frames.text: bearing bolts.

frames.name: p091-text-0363
frames.text: 4. Examine the connecting rod bearings for side play. The bush-

frames.name: p091-text-0364
frames.text: ing carried by the forked rod should have from 0.010 to 0.020 inch

frames.name: p091-text-0365
frames.text: side play on the crank pin. This may be checked with a thickness

frames.name: p091-text-0366
frames.text: gauge. The plain end connecting rod should have from 0.004 to

frames.name: p091-text-0367
frames.text: 0.008 inch side play in the forked rod.

frames.name: p091-text-0368
frames.text: 5. Remove each pair of connecting rods by first taking off the nuts

frames.name: p091-text-0369
frames.text: No. 13251 and the cap of the plain end rod, then take off nuts No.

frames.name: p091-text-0370
frames.text: 13220 and the caps of the forked end rod.

frames.name: p091-text-0371
frames.text: Note.—That the caps and rods are each numbered at the joint
frames.pdf_text: NOTE.—That the caps and rods are each numbered at the joint

frames.name: p091-text-0372
frames.text: on one side. The caps should always be replaced on the rod with

frames.name: p091-text-0373
frames.text: like numbers adjacent. The bushings are also marked with small

frames.name: p091-text-0374
frames.text: Plate No. 57

frames.name: p091-text-0375
frames.text: CONNECTING RODS

frames.name: p092-text-0377
frames.text: numbers on the flange. These numbers should always be adjacent

frames.name: p092-text-0378
frames.text: and on the side of the rod which bears the cap numbers. Each con-

frames.name: p092-text-0379
frames.text: necting rod is also numbered on the web near the piston-pin end.

frames.name: p092-text-0380
frames.text: The upper number at this point indicates the serial number of the

frames.name: p092-text-0381
frames.text: crank shaft to which the rods have been fitted. The lower number

frames.name: p092-text-0382
frames.text: indicates the position of the rod in the engine, as 1, 2, 3, etc., number-

frames.name: p092-text-0383
frames.text: ing from the distributor end of the engine.

frames.name: p092-text-0384
frames.text: 6. Examine the crank-pin bushing carefully. It should show a 75

frames.name: p092-text-0385
frames.text: per cent bearing free from dirt and scratches or scores. Any dirt or

frames.name: p092-text-0386
frames.text: foreign matter should be carefully scraped out. The outside of the

frames.name: p092-text-0387
frames.text: crank-pin bushing on which the plain end rod bears should also be care-

frames.name: p092-text-0388
frames.text: fully examined. Any roughness on its surface should be dressed down

frames.name: p092-text-0389
frames.text: with a fine mill file. Oil grooves and oil holes should be cleaned out.

frames.name: p092-text-0390
frames.text: FITTING CONNECTING-ROD BEARINGS

frames.name: p092-text-0391
frames.text: If the bearing has been damaged or shows wear to such an extent

frames.name: p092-text-0392
frames.text: that it is advisable to replace it, the new bushings should first be

frames.name: p092-text-0393
frames.text: fitted in the forked end rod. Be sure that the bushing seats properly

frames.name: p092-text-0394
frames.text: in the rod and that the dowel does not hold it away at any point.

frames.name: p092-text-0395
frames.text: The caps of the forked end rod should be put in place and drawn up

frames.name: p092-text-0396
frames.text: tightly. Examine the joints between the cap and the rod and between

frames.name: p092-text-0397
frames.text: the two halves of the bushings. Caps and bushings should bear

frames.name: p092-text-0398
frames.text: equally hard at the joints. The bushings should then be scraped

frames.name: p092-text-0399
frames.text: to a free fit on a mandrel 0.003 to 0.004 inch larger than the crank pin.

frames.name: p092-text-0400
frames.text: The cap should now be removed and the rod tried on the crank pin

frames.name: p092-text-0401
frames.text: on which it is to run. The ends of the bushing should be dressed

frames.name: p092-text-0402
frames.text: off with a fine mill file and a sufficient amount removed to permit

frames.name: p092-text-0403
frames.text: from 0.010 to 0.020 inch side play. Touch up the radius at each end

frames.name: p092-text-0404
frames.text: of the bushing with a scraper until it clears the fillet of the crank pin.

frames.name: p092-text-0405
frames.text: Test this point by coating the crank pin and each fillet lightly with

frames.name: p092-text-0406
frames.text: red lead or Prussian blue.

frames.name: p092-text-0407
frames.text: Clamp the rod with its bushing on the crank pin. Revolve it on the

frames.name: p092-text-0408
frames.text: crank pin two or three times, meanwhile pressing it first toward one

frames.name: p092-text-0409
frames.text: end of the crank pin and then toward the other end. Remove the

frames.name: p092-text-0410
frames.text: rod and carefully scrape off any high spots to which the color has been

frames.name: p092-text-0411
frames.text: transferred. It is very essential that these bushings do not bear on

frames.name: p092-text-0412
frames.text: the fillet.

frames.name: p092-text-0413
frames.text: 7. With the bushing clamped in the forked end rod dress down the

frames.name: p092-text-0414
frames.text: outside surface at the joints with a fine mill file until they are per-

frames.name: p092-text-0415
frames.text: fectly smooth. Coat the bearing surfaces of the plain end rod lightly

frames.name: p092-text-0416
frames.text: with red lead or Prussian blue and fit it in place on the bushing. Any

frames.name: p092-text-0417
frames.text: high spots on the bearing to which the color is transferred should be

frames.name: p092-text-0418
frames.text: dressed down until the plain end rod has 0.005 to 0.0065 inch diamet-

frames.name: p092-text-0419
frames.text: rical clearance. The roundness of the bushing should meanwhile be

frames.name: p092-text-0420
frames.text: tested with micrometers.

frames.name: p093-text-0422
frames.text: Determine whether or not the

frames.name: p093-text-0423
frames.text: mandrels lie in the same plane by

frames.name: p093-text-0424
frames.text: laying them on parallel bars on a

frames.name: p093-text-0425
frames.text: surface plate.

frames.name: p093-text-0426
frames.text: Check the distance between the

frames.name: p093-text-0427
frames.text: mandrels at each end by means of

frames.name: p093-text-0428
frames.text: a gauge as shown.

frames.name: p093-text-0429
frames.text: To straighten a rod clamp it in a

frames.name: p093-text-0430
frames.text: vise between blocks to protect the

frames.name: p093-text-0431
frames.text: flanges.

frames.name: p093-text-0432
frames.text: To determine the diametrical clearance which a connecting-rod

frames.name: p093-text-0433
frames.text: bearing has, the crank pin and the outside of the connecting-rod bush-

frames.name: p093-text-0434
frames.text: ing should be carefully measured with micrometers. The connecting

frames.name: p093-text-0435
frames.text: rods should then be clamped on to test mandrels, the diameter of

frames.name: p093-text-0436
frames.text: which may readily be determined. Connecting-rod bearings should

frames.name: p093-text-0437
frames.text: be fitted at base repair shops equipped with a complete set of such

frames.name: p093-text-0438
frames.text: mandrels.

frames.name: p093-text-0439
frames.text: 8. Examine the bushing at the top end of the connecting rod. This

frames.name: p093-text-0440
frames.text: should show a burnished bearing surface free from scratches or scores.

frames.name: p093-text-0441
frames.text: The radial clearance of this bushing and its proper piston pin should

frames.name: p093-text-0442
frames.text: be 0.001 inch. If it has been necessary to replace this bushing, the

frames.name: p093-text-0443
frames.text: new one should be oiled on its outside surface and carefully pressed

frames.name: p093-text-0444
frames.text: into place under an arbor press or in a vise. After being pressed into

frames.name: p093-text-0445
frames.text: place it should be reamed with an expansion reamer until it has the

frames.name: p093-text-0446
frames.text: proper clearance on the piston pin.

frames.name: p093-text-0447
frames.text: Plate No. 58

frames.name: p093-text-0448
frames.text: Plate No. 59

frames.name: p093-text-0449
frames.text: Plate No. 60

frames.name: p093-text-0450
frames.text: ALIGNING RODS

frames.name: p094-text-0452
frames.text: ALIGNING CONNECTING RODS

frames.name: p094-text-0453
frames.text: When new bushings are fitted in a connecting rod, or if an inspec-

frames.name: p094-text-0454
frames.text: tion of the piston would indicate that the connecting rod was twisted

frames.name: p094-text-0455
frames.text: or bent, the rod should be checked for alignment in the following

frames.name: p094-text-0456
frames.text: manner. A snug-fitting mandrel should be put through the bearing

frames.name: p094-text-0457
frames.text: in each end of the rod. These mandrels should be at least 12 inches

frames.name: p094-text-0458
frames.text: long. The rod with the mandrels in place should be laid on a surface

frames.name: p094-text-0459
frames.text: plate and the mandrels checked as to whether or not they are parallel

frames.name: p094-text-0460
frames.text: and in the same plane, as illustrated on page 93. A twisted or bent

frames.name: p094-text-0461
frames.text: rod may be straightened by clamping one end of it in a heavy vise and

frames.name: p094-text-0462
frames.text: springing it with a bending bar. A rod which has been badly bent

frames.name: p094-text-0463
frames.text: should not be used, nor should it be heated in order to facilitate

frames.name: p094-text-0464
frames.text: straightening.

frames.name: p094-text-0465
frames.text: CRANK SHAFT

frames.name: p094-text-0466
frames.text: After the connecting rods have been inspected, overhauled, and

frames.name: p094-text-0467
frames.text: laid to one side, the crank shaft may be lifted out of its bearings.

frames.name: p094-text-0468
frames.text: All bearing surfaces on the crank shaft should be carefully examined.

frames.name: p094-text-0469
frames.text: Unless one or more of the bearings have been completely destroyed,

frames.name: p094-text-0470
frames.text: the crank-shaft surface will be in good condition.

frames.name: p094-text-0471
frames.text: If any crank pin or bearing surface on the crank shaft is roughened

frames.name: p094-text-0472
frames.text: or scored, it should be dressed down with a fine mill file and fine

frames.name: p094-text-0473
frames.text: sandpaper and oil, meanwhile being tested as to roundness with a

frames.name: p094-text-0474
frames.text: micrometer.

frames.name: p094-text-0475
frames.text: Examine the ball thrust bearing. This should show not to exceed

frames.name: p094-text-0476
frames.text: 0.008 inch end play. Unless the thrust bearing shows damage or

frames.name: p094-text-0477
frames.text: excessive end play after being washed, it should not be necessary to

frames.name: p094-text-0478
frames.text: remove it. Be sure that it is packed with grease before engine is

frames.name: p094-text-0479
frames.text: finally assembled.

frames.name: p094-text-0480
frames.text: Examine the lock screw through the thrust-bearing retaining nut.

frames.name: p094-text-0481
frames.text: Be sure that it is tightly drawn up and that the lock wire sets fairly

frames.name: p094-text-0482
frames.text: in the slot.

frames.name: p094-text-0483
frames.text: If it is considered advisable to remove the clutch shaft, follow the

frames.name: p094-text-0484
frames.text: instructions given on page 118.

frames.name: p094-text-0485
frames.text: Examine the tapered end of the shaft on which the clutch shaft

frames.name: p094-text-0486
frames.text: fits. If this has been marred or roughened up in any way the key

frames.name: p094-text-0487
frames.text: should be removed and the rough spot smoothed up.

frames.name: p094-text-0488
frames.text: The connection should then be lapped.

frames.name: p094-text-0489
frames.text: Examine the condition of the key and its fit in the shaft.

frames.name: p094-text-0490
frames.text: Examine the crank-shaft gear to see that it does not show excessive

frames.name: p094-text-0491
frames.text: wear.

frames.name: p094-text-0492
frames.text: Examine the plug in the clutch end of the shaft and the plugs in

frames.name: p094-text-0493
frames.text: the ends of each main bearing and crank pin. They should all be

frames.name: p094-text-0494
frames.text: tight and show no indications of oil leakage.

frames.name: p094-text-0495
frames.text: Clean out the oil cavities and passages in the crank shaft and

frames.name: p094-text-0496
frames.text: crank pins. This can best be done by filling each one with gasoline

frames.name: p094-text-0497
frames.text: or kerosene, allowing it to stand for a short time and then blowing

frames.name: p094-text-0498
frames.text: out with compressed air.

frames.name: p096-text-0540
frames.text: CRANK CASE

frames.name: p096-text-0541
frames.text: Examine all bearing bushings in both the upper and lower halves of

frames.name: p096-text-0542
frames.text: the crank case. The bushings should show a 75 per cent bearing and

frames.name: p096-text-0543
frames.text: should be free from dirt, scratches, and scores. Should it be neces-

frames.name: p096-text-0544
frames.text: sary to replace any of these bearings, new bushings should be care-

frames.name: p096-text-0545
frames.text: fully fitted in each half of the crank case. They should then be

frames.name: p096-text-0546
frames.text: carefully scraped to a free fit on a mandrel 0.0025 inch to 0.00325

frames.name: p096-text-0547
frames.text: inch larger in diameter than the crank shaft.

frames.name: p096-text-0548
frames.text: In scraping the bushings to a fit on this mandrel, care should be

frames.name: p096-text-0549
frames.text: taken that the case is supported and clamped down in such a manner

frames.name: p096-text-0550
frames.text: that it will not be sprung or twisted out of shape. It is advisable to

frames.name: p096-text-0551
frames.text: clamp the case at only one point and that only rigidly enough to

frames.name: p096-text-0552
frames.text: hold it steady. Contact between the two halves of the bushing and

frames.name: p096-text-0553
frames.text: the two halves of the crank case should be equal when they are

frames.name: p096-text-0554
frames.text: clamped together.

frames.name: p096-text-0555
frames.text: Examine the crank-shaft bearing bolts and see that the nuts at

frames.name: p096-text-0556
frames.text: the lower end of these bolts are drawn up tightly and properly

frames.name: p096-text-0557
frames.text: cotter pinned.

frames.name: p096-text-0558
frames.text: Examine the threads on the top of these bolts to see that they are

frames.name: p096-text-0559
frames.text: not stripped.

frames.name: p096-text-0560
frames.text: Wash the inside of the case thoroughly and clean and blow out all

frames.name: p096-text-0561
frames.text: oil passages. Extreme care should be exercised in carrying out this

frames.name: p096-text-0562
frames.text: part of the work.

frames.name: p096-text-0563
frames.text: Caution.—The joint between the two halves of the case is “lapped”

frames.name: p096-text-0564
frames.text: and the parts should be carefully handled to avoid possibility of

frames.name: p096-text-0565
frames.text: marring the surfaces.

frames.text: COOLING SYSTEM

frames.name: p097-text-0569
frames.text: The engine-cooling system on this tank is comprised of a tubular

frames.name: p097-text-0570
frames.text: type of radiator, a Sirocco blower fan, and the water pump which

frames.name: p097-text-0571
frames.text: maintains circulation. There is an auxiliary tank adjoining the

frames.name: p097-text-0572
frames.text: radiator. The radiator is placed horizontally, just aft of the engine

frames.name: p097-text-0573
frames.text: on the port side of the hull, near the top of the engine compartment.

frames.name: p097-text-0574
frames.text: The water is circulated through the jackets, and thence to the radia-

frames.name: p097-text-0575
frames.text: tors by the pump described on page 98. The air for cooling is

frames.name: p097-text-0576
frames.text: forced through the radiator by the ventilating system, which draws

frames.name: p097-text-0577
frames.text: air through a louver in the top of the machine, just aft of the main

frames.name: p097-text-0578
frames.text: turret. The air is drawn through the air ducts and forced through

frames.name: p097-text-0579
frames.text: the outlet louver, which is located aft of the inlet louver, by the

frames.name: p097-text-0580
frames.text: Sirocco fan, having a capacity of 11,000 cubic feet of air per minute.

frames.name: p097-text-0581
frames.text: The radiator has 296 tubes, 38

frames.name: p097-text-0585
frames.text: inches in length of seamless drawn

frames.name: p097-text-0586
frames.text: copper tubing, giving an actual area of 12,902 square inches or 89.5

frames.name: p097-text-0587
frames.text: square feet.

frames.name: p097-text-0588
frames.text: Plate No. 64

frames.name: p097-text-0589
frames.text: PIPE INSTALLATION

frames.name: p098-text-0592
frames.text: The Sirocco blower is driven by means of a link belt from the

frames.name: p098-text-0593
frames.text: engine to a bevel gear box, and from the bevel gear box to the fan

frames.name: p098-text-0594
frames.text: shaft by means of a V belt. The ratio of the crank shaft to the

frames.name: p098-text-0595
frames.text: blower shaft is 1.561 to 1.

frames.name: p098-text-0596
frames.text: TO REMOVE THE RADIATOR

frames.name: p098-text-0597
frames.text: Unbolt and remove the air ducts. Disconnect the water, drain, and

frames.name: p098-text-0598
frames.text: steam pipes. Unbolt the front and rear radiator support brackets.

frames.name: p098-text-0599
frames.text: Remove the radiator through the outlet louver. For access to the

frames.name: p098-text-0600
frames.text: work the side plates along the side of the epicyclic gear and the outlet

frames.name: p098-text-0601
frames.text: louver should be removed before starting the work.

frames.name: p098-text-0602
frames.text: TO REMOVE THE SIROCCO FAN

frames.name: p098-text-0603
frames.text: Disconnect the driving belts and allow the jockey pulley to lay on

frames.name: p098-text-0604
frames.text: the floor. Unbolt the air ducts attached to the fan. Remove the

frames.name: p098-text-0605
frames.text: handhole plate on the side of the hull, opposite the fan-rotor spindle,

frames.name: p098-text-0606
frames.text: by unscrewing the bolts.

frames.name: p098-text-0607
frames.text: Remove the nuts at the inner end of spindle and take off driving

frames.name: p098-text-0608
frames.text: pulley, removing outer nut and ball race. Draw spindle out through

frames.name: p098-text-0609
frames.text: the handhole.

frames.name: p098-text-0610
frames.text: Take off the legs (bolted to floor and engine frame) and remove fan

frames.name: p098-text-0611
frames.text: through engine-room bulkhead door. After getting it into the fight-

frames.name: p098-text-0612
frames.text: ing compartment, turn it around to pass through the side door of

frames.name: p098-text-0613
frames.text: fighting compartment.

frames.name: p098-text-0614
frames.text: ENGINE-COOLING SYSTEM

frames.name: p098-text-0615
frames.text: Cooling water is circulated through the Liberty engine by means

frames.name: p098-text-0616
frames.text: of a centrifugal pump running at one and one-half times engine

frames.name: p098-text-0617
frames.text: speed. The capacity of this pump is 100 gallons per minute at 1,700

frames.name: p098-text-0618
frames.text: r. p. m. The cooling system from the pump inlet to and including

frames.name: p098-text-0619
frames.text: the water-outlet header will hold 5½ gallons of water.

frames.name: p098-text-0620
frames.text: The water pump is provided with a single inlet, the outside diame-

frames.name: p098-text-0621
frames.text: ter of which is 2 inches, and two outlets, each one delivering water

frames.name: p098-text-0622
frames.text: to a header supplying the right and left hand cylinders, respectively.

frames.name: p098-text-0623
frames.text: Water is forced into each cylinder-jacket tangent to its outside sur-

frames.name: p098-text-0624
frames.text: face. This construction gives the water a whirling motion inside the

frames.name: p098-text-0625
frames.text: jacket and insures uniform cooling.

frames.name: p098-text-0626
frames.text: The water-outlet pipe for each cylinder extends inside the jacket

frames.name: p098-text-0627
frames.text: to a point very close to the exhaust-valve chamber, which guarantees

frames.name: p098-text-0628
frames.text: the proper cooling of the exhaust valve. The cooling water then goes

frames.name: p098-text-0629
frames.text: through a passage cored in the intake headers. This serves to warm

frames.name: p098-text-0630
frames.text: and further vaporize the incoming gas as well as assist in cooling the

frames.name: p098-text-0631
frames.text: water. These passages in the intake headers are connected by two

frames.name: p098-text-0632
frames.text: water-outlet headers, the final outlet of which has an outside diameter

frames.name: p098-text-0633
frames.text: of 2 inches.

frames.name: p099-text-0635
frames.text: DISASSEMBLING AND INSPECTION

frames.name: p099-text-0636
frames.text: Loosen the hose clamps No. 8453 and pull the hose off the pump:

frames.name: p099-text-0637
frames.text: Loosen the hose clamps No. 8450 and remove the water inlet mani-

frames.name: p099-text-0638
frames.text: folds No. 12123 with the cylinder hose connections No. 8152 and the

frames.name: p099-text-0639
frames.text: extensions No. 12096 and No. 12097 with their hose connections. All

frames.name: p099-text-0640
frames.text: rubber hose should be carefully examined for defects—especially on

frames.name: p099-text-0641
frames.text: the inside. It sometimes happens that the inside layer of rubber will

frames.name: p099-text-0642
frames.text: become loosened and will wholly or partially obstruct the passage.

frames.name: p099-text-0643
frames.text: 1. Remove four nuts No. 103 and washers No. 113. This will per-

frames.name: p099-text-0644
frames.text: mit the water pump to be dismounted from the engine.

frames.name: p099-text-0645
frames.text: 2. Remove eight nuts No. 101 and the washers No. 111 and take

frames.name: p099-text-0646
frames.text: off the water pump cover No. 12078.

frames.name: p099-text-0647
frames.text: 3. Remove nut No. 8214 from the end of the water-pump shaft and

frames.name: p099-text-0648
frames.text: draw off impeller by means of the special tool.

frames.name: p099-text-0649
frames.text: 4. Now lift the key No. 159, which will permit the water pump to

frames.name: p099-text-0650
frames.text: be withdrawn.

frames.name: p099-text-0651
frames.text: Plate No. 65.

frames.name: p099-text-0652
frames.text: FAN BEVEL GEAR DRIVE

frames.name: p100-text-0654
frames.text: 5. Examine the water-pump shaft. If it is rusted to such an extent

frames.name: p100-text-0655
frames.text: that it is very rough it should be replaced. Examine key and key seat.

frames.name: p100-text-0656
frames.text: 6. Examine the impeller to see that it has not been bent or dam-

frames.name: p100-text-0657
frames.text: aged in any way.

frames.name: p100-text-0658
frames.text: 7. Examine bearing No. 8056. This should be allowed end play to

frames.name: p100-text-0659
frames.text: extent of 0.005 inch.

frames.name: p100-text-0660
frames.text: TO REASSEMBLE

frames.name: p100-text-0661
frames.text: 1. Put the pump shaft with its bearing in place in the container No.

frames.name: p100-text-0662
frames.text: 8069. It would be advisable to use new packing in the packing boxes.

frames.name: p100-text-0663
frames.text: A

frames.name: p100-text-0667
frames.text: -inch soft round tope tweed packing is recommended for this

frames.name: p100-text-0668
frames.text: place, impregnated with a graphite grease. A piece approximately

frames.name: p100-text-0669
frames.text: 8½ inches long will be required for each packing box.

frames.name: p100-text-0670
frames.text: 2. One piece of this packing should now be wrapped around the

frames.name: p100-text-0671
frames.text: shaft and the gland No. 8059 put in place and pressed down until the

frames.name: p100-text-0672
frames.text: packing is properly seated.

frames.name: p100-text-0673
frames.text: 3. Compress the coil spring No. 8058 and fasten it in the compressed

frames.name: p100-text-0674
frames.text: state, on opposite sides, by means of twine or soft wire.

frames.name: p100-text-0675
frames.text: 4. Now slip the spring in place on the shaft.

frames.name: p100-text-0676
frames.text: 5. Put on the second gland No. 8059 and another piece of packing

frames.name: p100-text-0678
frames.text: 6. Water-pump body No. 12071 should now be put in place, the key

frames.name: p100-text-0679
frames.text: No. 159 inserted in the key seat in the shaft and the impeller No.

frames.name: p100-text-0680
frames.text: 12073 drawn up into place by means of the nut No. 8214.

frames.name: p100-text-0681
frames.text: 7. The wire or string holding the spring in the compressed state

frames.name: p100-text-0682
frames.text: must now be cut and drawn out. With the water-pump body and

frames.name: p100-text-0683
frames.text: the bearing container clamped tightly together the shaft and the

frames.name: p100-text-0684
frames.text: impeller should turn freely. The permissible end play in the water-

frames.name: p100-text-0685
frames.text: pump shaft is 0.010 inch.

frames.name: p100-text-0686
frames.text: 8. Put the gasket No. 8215 in place. This should be replaced if it

frames.name: p100-text-0687
frames.text: has been at all damaged in disassembling.

frames.name: p100-text-0688
frames.text: 9. Complete the assembly by putting the water-pump cover in

frames.name: p100-text-0689
frames.text: place with its washers and nuts. Be sure that these are all evenly

frames.name: p100-text-0690
frames.text: drawn up and properly cotter pinned.

frames.name: p100-text-0691
frames.text: WATER-PUMP BEVEL DRIVER

frames.name: p100-text-0692
frames.text: Remove screw No. 154. This will permit the bevel driver and

frames.name: p100-text-0693
frames.text: housing assembly to be withdrawn through the opening in the bottom

frames.name: p100-text-0694
frames.text: of the crank case which receives the oil pump.

frames.name: p100-text-0695
frames.text: Remove the two clamp bolts No. 116.

frames.name: p100-text-0696
frames.text: Examine the shaft of the bevel driver and the bushing in which it

frames.name: p100-text-0697
frames.text: runs. Both should be free from scores and indications of cutting.

frames.name: p100-text-0698
frames.text: Remove any dirt in the bushing with a scraper. End play of the

frames.name: p100-text-0699
frames.text: driver in its bearing should be from 0.005 to 0.008 inch. Diametrical

frames.name: p100-text-0700
frames.text: clearance should be 0.0015 to 0.0025 inch.
